bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第199卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 199
translations.idiomatic: Volume 199 of the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十五】起著雍涒灘四月，盡閼蒙單閼九月，凡七年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records, Fifteen] Beginning in the fourth month of the year Zhu Yong Cui Tan, ending in the ninth month of the year Yan Meng Dan Yan—in all, somewhat more than seven years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Fifteen] From the fourth month of the Zhu Yong Cui Tan year-cycle through the ninth month of the Yan Meng Dan Yan cycle—a span of a little more than seven years.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，右武候將軍梁建方擊松外蠻，破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day dingsi, Right Martial Sentinel General Liang Jianfang attacked the Songwai barbarians and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day dingsi, Right Martial Sentinel General Liang Jianfang attacked the Songwai tribes and routed them.

sentences.zh: 初，巂州都督劉伯英上言：「松外諸蠻暫降復叛，請出師討之，以通西洱、天竺之道。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi Prefecture Protector-General Liu Boying memorialized the throne: "The various Songwai barbarians have submitted for a time and then rebelled again. I request that troops be sent to punish them, so as to open the route to Western Er and India."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Protector-General Liu Boying of Xi Prefecture had memorialized: "The Songwai tribes keep surrendering only to rebel again. I ask that an expedition be sent against them to secure the road west to Er River and on to India."

sentences.zh: 敕建方發巴蜀十二州兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jianfang to mobilize troops from the twelve Ba-Shu prefectures to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jianfang to raise troops from the twelve Ba-Shu prefectures for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋雙捨帥眾拒戰，建方擊敗之，殺獲千餘人。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Shuangshe led his people to resist; Jianfang defeated them, killing and capturing more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leader Shuangshe led his warriors into battle; Jianfang broke them and killed or captured over a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 群蠻震懾，亡竄山谷。

translations.literal: The mass of barbarians were shaken with fear and fled into the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The other tribes were terrified and scattered into the hills.

sentences.zh: 建方分遣使者諭以利害，皆來歸附，前後至者七十部，戶十萬九千三百，建方署其酋長蒙和等為縣令，各統所部，莫不感悅。

translations.literal: Jianfang sent envoys in separate parties to explain advantage and harm; all came to submit. In all, seventy groups arrived, with 109,300 households. Jianfang appointed their chieftains Meng He and others as district magistrates, each ruling his own people; none failed to be moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfang then sent envoys to explain what submission would gain them and what resistance would cost; tribes came in one after another until seventy groups, numbering 109,300 households, had submitted. He appointed chiefs such as Meng He as district magistrates over their own people, and all were deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 因遣使詣西洱河，其帥楊盛大駭，具船將遁，使者曉諭以威信，盛遂請降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to Western Er River; its leader Yang Sheng was greatly alarmed, prepared boats and was about to flee. The envoys enlightened him with the court's prestige and authority, and Sheng then requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to the Western Er River region. Its chief Yang Sheng was terrified and began fitting out boats to escape, but the envoys persuaded him with the court's power and promise of favor, and Sheng asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 其地有楊、李、趙、董等數十姓，各據一州，大者六百，小者二、三百戶，無大君長，不相統壹，語雖小訛，其生業、風俗，大略與中國同，自雲本皆華人，其所異者以十二月為歲首。

translations.literal: In that region there were several tens of surnames such as Yang, Li, Zhao, and Dong; each held one district. The large had six hundred households, the small two or three hundred. There was no great lord or chief, and they did not unite under one rule. Though their speech differed slightly, their livelihoods and customs were in the main the same as China's; they themselves said they were originally all Chinese. What differed was that they took the twelfth month as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The region held dozens of clans—Yang, Li, Zhao, Dong, and others—each occupying its own district, the largest with six hundred households, the smallest with two or three hundred. They had no paramount chief and did not form a single polity. Their dialects diverged only slightly from Chinese, and their livelihoods and customs were largely the same; they claimed to be Chinese by origin, differing chiefly in reckoning the year from the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 己未，契丹辱紇主曲據帥眾內附。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, the Khitan Rouruo chieftain Quju led his people to submit and enter allegiance within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Quju, chieftain of the Khitan Rouruo, led his people to submit to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 以其地置玄州，以曲據為刺史，隸營州都督府。

translations.literal: His territory was made into Xuan Prefecture, with Quju as prefect, subordinate to the Yingzhou Protectorate-General.
translations.idiomatic: The court established Xuan Prefecture on his lands, appointed Quju prefect, and placed the prefecture under the Yingzhou protectorate.

sentences.zh: 甲子，烏胡鎮將古神感將兵浮海擊高麗，遇高麗步騎五千，戰於易山，破之。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Wuhu Garrison commander Gu Shendian led troops by sea to attack Goguryeo. He encountered five thousand Goguryeo infantry and cavalry, fought at Yishan, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Gu Shendian, commander of Wuhu Garrison, sailed against Goguryeo with a naval force. He met five thousand Goguryeo foot and horse at Mount Yi, defeated them, and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 其夜，高麗萬餘人襲神感船，神感設伏，又破之而還。

translations.literal: That night, more than ten thousand Goguryeo troops raided Shendian's ships. Shendian set an ambush and again defeated them, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night more than ten thousand Goguryeo soldiers attacked his fleet by surprise; Shendian laid an ambush, routed them again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，西突厥乙毘咄陸可汗以阿史那賀魯為葉護，居多邏斯水，在西州北千五百里，統處月、處密、始蘇、歌邏祿、失畢五姓之眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Western Türk qaghan Yipiduolu had made Ashina Helu yabghu; he dwelt at Duoluo River, fifteen hundred li north of Xizhou, ruling the peoples of the five clans: Chuyue, Chumi, Shisu, Geluolu, and Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Western Türk qaghan Yipiduolu had appointed Ashina Helu as yabghu. Helu held Duoluo River, fifteen hundred li north of Xizhou, and commanded the five tribal confederations of Chuyue, Chumi, Shisu, Geluolu, and Shibi.

sentences.zh: 乙毘咄陸奔吐火羅，乙毘射匱可汗遣兵迫逐之，部落亡散。

translations.literal: Yipiduolu fled to Tuhuoluo; the qaghan Yipishegui sent troops to pursue him, and the tribes scattered and were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Yipiduolu fled to Tuhuoluo, Qaghan Yipishegui sent troops in pursuit, and Helu's tribes broke apart and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，賀魯帥其餘眾數千帳內屬，詔處之於庭州莫賀城，拜左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Helu led his remaining people of several thousand tents to submit within the borders. An edict settled them at Mohe City in Ting Prefecture and appointed him Left Swift-Cavalry Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Helu led the several thousand tents that remained to submit to the Tang. The court settled them at Mohe City in Ting Prefecture and appointed Helu general of the Left Swift-Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 賀魯聞唐兵討龜茲，請為鄉導，仍從數十騎入朝。

translations.literal: When Helu heard that Tang troops were campaigning against Kucha, he asked to serve as guide and still came to court with several tens of horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Tang forces were marching on Kucha, Helu offered to guide them and came to court with a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 上以為昆丘道行軍總管，厚宴賜而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor made him campaign commander of the Kunqiu Route, gave him a lavish feast and gifts, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him commander of the Kunqiu Route army, entertained him generously, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚子，右衛率長史王玄策擊帝那伏帝王阿羅那順，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengzi, Chief Secretary of the Right Guard Command Wang Xuance attacked the emperor of Central India, Aruonashun, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day gengzi, Wang Xuance, chief secretary of the Right Guard Command, attacked Aruonashun, the self-proclaimed king of Central India, and crushed his army.

sentences.zh: 初，中天竺王屍羅逸多兵最強，四天竺皆臣之，玄策奉使至天竺，諸國皆遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, the king of Central India, Shiluoyiduo, had the strongest army; the four Indias all served him. When Xuance went on mission to India, every state sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shiluoyiduo of Central India had been the strongest ruler in the region, and the other three Indias had all acknowledged him. When Xuance arrived on an embassy, each state sent tribute missions to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 會屍羅逸多卒，國中大亂，其臣阿羅那順自立，發胡兵攻玄策；

translations.literal: When Shiluoyiduo died, the state fell into great disorder. His minister Aruonashun declared himself ruler and raised foreign troops to attack Xuance;
translations.idiomatic: Then Shiluoyiduo died, the realm fell into chaos, and his minister Aruonashun seized power and sent foreign troops against Xuance;

sentences.zh: 玄策帥從者三十人與戰，力不敵，悉為所擒，阿羅那順盡掠諸國貢物。

translations.literal: Xuance led his thirty attendants into battle but was not equal in strength; all were captured. Aruonashun plundered all the tribute goods of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance fought with his thirty attendants but was overwhelmed; all were taken prisoner, and Aruonashun seized the tribute goods the embassies were carrying.

sentences.zh: 玄策脫身宵遁，抵吐蕃西境，以書征鄰國兵，吐蕃遣精銳千二百人、泥婆國遣七千餘騎赴之。

translations.literal: Xuance escaped by night, reached the western border of Tibet, and by letter summoned troops from neighboring states. Tibet sent twelve hundred elite soldiers; Nepal sent more than seven thousand cavalry to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance slipped away by night, reached the Tibetan frontier, and called on neighboring states for aid by letter. Tibet sent twelve hundred picked troops, and Nepal more than seven thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 玄策與其副蔣師仁帥二國之兵，進至中天竺所居茶餺和羅城，連戰三日，大破之，斬首三千餘級，赴水溺死者且萬人。

translations.literal: Xuance and his deputy Jiang Shiren led the troops of the two states forward to Chabohuoluo City where Central India dwelt. They fought for three days straight and won a great victory, beheading more than three thousand; those who drowned fleeing into the water were nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance and his deputy Jiang Shiren led the combined armies to Chabohuoluo, the capital of Central India. After three days of fighting they won a decisive victory, taking more than three thousand heads and drowning nearly ten thousand of the enemy in the rivers.

sentences.zh: 阿羅那順棄城走，更收餘眾，還與師仁戰；

translations.literal: Aruonashun abandoned the city and fled, gathered his remaining forces again, and returned to fight Shiren;
translations.idiomatic: Aruonashun abandoned the city and fled, but rallied his remnants and attacked Shiren again;

sentences.zh: 又破之，擒阿羅那順。

translations.literal: They defeated him again and captured Aruonashun.
translations.idiomatic: they defeated him once more and took Aruonashun prisoner.

sentences.zh: 餘眾奉其妃及王子，阻乾陀衛江，師仁進擊之，眾潰，獲其妃及王子，虜男女萬二千人。

translations.literal: The remaining troops supported his consort and prince, blocking the Gandhara guard river. Shiren advanced to attack; the masses collapsed. He captured the consort and prince and took captive twelve thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors rallied around his queen and prince and held the Gandhara frontier river. Shiren attacked, broke them, captured the queen and prince, and took twelve thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 於是天竺響震，城邑聚落降者五百八十餘所，俘阿羅那順以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon India trembled at the report; more than five hundred eighty walled cities and settlements submitted. They brought Aruonashun captive back.
translations.idiomatic: All India was shaken; more than five hundred eighty towns and settlements submitted, and the victors brought Aruonashun back to the Tang as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 以玄策為朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Xuance was made Palace Attendant Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance was appointed Palace Attendant Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，以白別部為居延州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yichou, the Baibie tribe was made Juyan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day yichou, the Baibie tribe was organized as Juyan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，特進宋公蕭瑀卒，太常議謚曰「德」，尚書議謚曰「肅」。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Special Advancement Duke Xiao Yu of Song died. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name "Virtuous"; the Ministry of State Affairs proposed "Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, Xiao Yu, Duke of Song with the rank of Special Advancement, died. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous epithet Virtuous; the Ministry of State Affairs proposed Solemn.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「謚者，行之跡，當得其實，可謚曰貞褊公。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A posthumous name is the trace of conduct; it should match the reality. He may be posthumously titled Duke of Upright Narrowness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A posthumous name records a man's conduct and must fit the truth. Let him be called Duke of Upright Narrowness."

sentences.zh: 子銳嗣，尚上女襄城公主。

translations.literal: His son Rui succeeded him and married the emperor's daughter, Princess Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui succeeded him and was married to the emperor's daughter, Princess Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 上欲為之營第，公主固辭，曰：「婦事舅姑，當朝夕侍側，若居別第，所闕多矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to build a separate mansion for them. The princess firmly declined, saying: "A wife serves her husband's parents and should attend them morning and evening. If she lives in a separate residence, how much is lacking!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to build them a separate mansion, but the princess firmly refused, saying, "A wife owes daily service to her husband's parents. A separate house would leave too much undone."

sentences.zh: 上乃命即瑀第而營之。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that construction be carried out right at Yu's own residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore ordered the work done within Xiao Yu's existing compound.

sentences.zh: 上以高麗困弊，議以明年發三十萬眾，一舉滅之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Goguryeo exhausted and impoverished, discussed sending three hundred thousand men the next year to destroy it in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Goguryeo exhausted, the emperor discussed raising three hundred thousand men the following year to destroy the kingdom in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 或以為大軍東征，須備經歲之糧，非畜乘所能載，宜具舟艦為水運。

translations.literal: Some held that a great army campaigning east would need provisions for a full year, which draft animals could not carry, and that ships should be prepared for transport by water.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that an eastern expedition would need a year's provisions—more than pack animals could carry—and that the army should rely on a fleet for supply by water.

sentences.zh: 隋末劍南獨無寇盜，屬者遼東之役，劍南復不預及，其百姓富庶，宜使之造舟艦。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, Jiannan alone had no bandits or robbers; in the recent Liaodong campaign, Jiannan again was not involved. Its common people were wealthy—they should be made to build ships.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Jiannan alone had escaped the turmoil of banditry, and it had been spared the recent Liaodong campaigns as well. Its people were prosperous and should be tasked with building the fleet.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，遣右領左右府長史強偉於劍南道伐木造舟艦，大者或長百尺，其廣半之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, he sent Chief Secretary of the Right Left and Right Leading Office Qiang Wei to the Jiannan circuit to fell timber and build ships; the largest were sometimes a hundred feet long, half as wide.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, he sent Qiang Wei, chief secretary of the Right Leading Office, to Jiannan to cut timber and build ships, some as long as a hundred feet and half as wide.

sentences.zh: 別遣使行水道，自巫峽抵江、揚，趣萊州。

translations.literal: He separately sent envoys to follow the water route from Wuxia Gorge to the Yangzi and Huai, pressing on to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to survey the water route from Wuxia Gorge down the Yangzi and Huai toward Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，西突厥相屈利啜請帥所部從討龜茲。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, the Western Türk chancellor Qulichuo asked to lead his division to follow in the attack on Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, Qulichuo, chancellor of the Western Türks, asked to lead his tribesmen in the campaign against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 初，左武衛將軍武連縣公武安李君羨直玄武門，時太白屢晝見，太史占云：「女主昌。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Martial Guard General Li Junxian, Duke of Wu'an in Wulian County, was on duty at the Xuanwu Gate. At that time Venus repeatedly appeared in daylight. The imperial astronomers divined: "The rule of a female sovereign will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Junxian, Duke of Wu'an and general of the Left Martial Guard, was stationed at the Xuanwu Gate. Venus had repeatedly been seen in daylight, and the court astronomers interpreted the omen: "A woman will rise to power."

sentences.zh: 民間又傳《秘記》云：「唐三世之後，女主武王代有天下。」

translations.literal: Among the people a Secret Record was also circulating that said: "After the third generation of Tang, a female sovereign surnamed Wu will replace Tang and possess the realm."
translations.idiomatic: A Secret Record was also circulating among the people: "After the third generation of Tang, a woman surnamed Wu will seize the realm."

sentences.zh: 上惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor detested this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loathed such talk.

sentences.zh: 會與諸武臣宴宮中，行酒令，使各言小名。

translations.literal: Once, when feasting in the palace with various martial ministers, they played a drinking game in which each had to speak his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a palace feast with his martial ministers, he had them play a drinking game in which each had to give his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 君羨自言名五娘，上愕然，因笑曰：「何物女子，乃爾勇健！」

translations.literal: Junxian himself said his name was Wuniang. The emperor was startled, then laughed and said: "What sort of woman is this, yet so bold and strong!"
translations.idiomatic: Junxian said his was Wuniang—"Fifth Daughter." The emperor started, then laughed and said, "What kind of woman is this, yet so fierce!"

sentences.zh: 又以君羨官稱封邑皆有「武」字，深惡之，後出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Junxian's official title and enfeoffment both contained the character "Wu," he deeply detested him and later transferred him out to be prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Because Junxian's title and fief both contained the character Wu, the emperor came to loathe him and later sent him out as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 有布衣員道信，自言能絕粒，曉佛法，君羨深敬信之，數相從，屏人語。

translations.literal: There was a commoner, Yuan Daoxin, who claimed he could abstain from grain, understood Buddhist teaching, and whom Junxian deeply revered and trusted. They often kept company and spoke apart from others.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Yuan Daoxin claimed he could live without grain and understood Buddhism. Junxian revered him, met with him often, and spoke with him in private.

sentences.zh: 御史奏君羨與妖人交通，謀不軌。

translations.literal: The censor memorialized that Junxian associated with a sorcerer and plotted sedition.
translations.idiomatic: The censors reported that Junxian was consorting with a sorcerer and plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，君羨坐誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Junxian was executed for his crime and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, Junxian was executed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 上密問太史令李淳風：「《秘記》所云，信有之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly asked Chief Astrologer Li Chunfeng: "What the Secret Record says—is it really so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly asked Chief Astrologer Li Chunfeng, "Can what the Secret Record says really come true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣仰稽天象，俯察歷數，其人已在陛下宮中，為親屬，自今不過三十年，當王天下，殺唐子孫殆盡，其兆既成矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant, looking up to examine the heavenly signs and looking down to scrutinize the calendrical numbers, finds that the person is already in Your Majesty's palace, a relative. From now it will be no more than thirty years before she rules the realm and kills Tang descendants almost to the last; the omen is already formed."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have read the heavens above and the calendrical signs below. The person is already in Your Majesty's palace, a kinswoman. Within thirty years she will rule the realm and slaughter the Tang line almost to extinction. The omen is already fixed."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「疑似者盡殺之，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If we kill everyone who is suspect, how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What if I killed everyone who might fit the prophecy?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天之所命，人不能違也。

translations.literal: He replied: "What Heaven has ordained, man cannot oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Li replied, "What Heaven has ordained, no man can overturn.

sentences.zh: 王者不死，徒多殺無辜。

translations.literal: One destined to be sovereign does not die; you would only kill many innocents in vain.
translations.idiomatic: A future sovereign cannot be killed off that way—you would only slaughter innocents in vain.

sentences.zh: 且自今以往三十年，其人已老，庶幾頗有慈心，為禍或淺。

translations.literal: Moreover, thirty years from now that person will be old; perhaps she will have some measure of compassion, and the harm may be slight.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, in thirty years she will be old and may show some mercy, so the harm may be less.

sentences.zh: 今借使得而殺之，天或生壯者肆其怨毒，恐陛下子孫，無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: If you were granted success in killing her now, Heaven might raise a younger person to vent fierce resentment, and I fear Your Majesty's descendants would be left with no survivors."
translations.idiomatic: If you killed her now and Heaven raised a younger successor filled with vengeance, I fear Your Majesty's line might be wiped out entirely."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 司空梁文昭公房玄齡留守京師，疾篤，上微赴玉華宮，肩輿入殿，至御座側乃下，相對流涕，因留宮下，聞其小愈則喜形於色，加劇則憂悴。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, Duke of Liang Wenzhao, remained to guard the capital and was gravely ill. The emperor went in light dress to Yuhua Palace, entered the hall in a shoulder carriage, and only descended at the side of the imperial seat. They faced each other in tears. He therefore stayed below the palace; when he heard of slight recovery his pleasure showed on his face, and when the illness worsened he was careworn.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, Duke of Liang Wenzhao and Minister of Works, had remained in the capital as regent and was gravely ill. The emperor went in informal dress to Yuhua Palace, was carried into the hall in a litter, and only stepped down beside the throne. They wept face to face, and the emperor stayed at the palace. News of slight improvement lit his face with joy; news of relapse left him haggard with worry.

sentences.zh: 玄齡謂諸子曰：「吾受主上厚恩，今天下無事，唯東征未已，群臣莫敢諫，吾知而不言，死有餘責。」

translations.literal: Xuanling told his sons: "I have received the sovereign's great grace. Today the realm is at peace, yet only the eastern expedition has not ceased. No minister dares remonstrate. I know this yet do not speak—death would still leave guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling told his sons, "The emperor has shown me extraordinary favor. The realm is at peace, yet the eastern expedition goes on and no minister dares speak against it. If I know this and stay silent, I deserve blame even in death."

sentences.zh: 乃上表諫，以為：「《老子》曰：『知足不辱，知止不殆。』

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial of remonstrance, holding: "Laozi says: 'To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial arguing, as Laozi said, "To know when one has enough is not to be shamed; to know when to stop is not to be ruined.

sentences.zh: 陛下功名威德亦可足矣，拓地開疆亦可止矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's achievements, fame, prestige, and virtue are already enough; expanding territory and opening frontiers may also cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's achievements, fame, and virtue are already enough; further conquest can stop.

sentences.zh: 且陛下每決一重囚，必令三覆五奏，進素膳，止音樂者，重人命也。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever Your Majesty decides a serious criminal case, you always order three reviews and five presentations, plain food brought in, and music stopped—this is to value human life.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Your Majesty condemns a serious offender, you require repeated review, take plain food, and halt music—because you value human life.

sentences.zh: 今驅無罪之士卒，委之鋒刃之下，使肝腦塗地，獨不足愍乎！

translations.literal: Now you drive innocent soldiers and cast them under sword's edge, making livers and brains smear the ground—is this alone not enough to pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you send innocent soldiers to die by the sword until the ground runs with their blood—is that not worth pity as well?

sentences.zh: 向使高麗違失臣節，誅之可也；

translations.literal: If Goguryeo had violated the duties of a subject, executing it would be permissible;
translations.idiomatic: If Goguryeo had broken its obligations as a vassal, punishment would be justified;

sentences.zh: 侵擾百姓，滅之可也；

translations.literal: if it had harassed the people, destroying it would be permissible;
translations.idiomatic: if it had ravaged your people, destruction would be justified;

sentences.zh: 他日能為中國患，除之可也。

translations.literal: if one day it could become a peril to China, removing it would be permissible.
translations.idiomatic: if one day it might threaten the empire, eliminating it would be justified.

sentences.zh: 今無此三條而坐煩中國，內為前代雪恥，外為新羅報仇，豈非所存者小，所損者太乎！

translations.literal: Now none of these three conditions exists, yet you trouble China for nothing—within, to wash away the shame of former dynasties; without, to avenge Silla. Is this not keeping what is small and losing what is great!
translations.idiomatic: None of these three conditions applies, yet you burden the empire—within, to avenge past dynasties; without, to fight Silla's war. Is this not grasping what is small and sacrificing what is great?

sentences.zh: 願陛下許高麗自新，焚陵波之船，罷應募之眾，自然華、夷慶賴，遠肅邇安。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would allow Goguryeo to reform itself, burn the ships at Lingbo, and dismiss the recruited masses; naturally Chinese and barbarian alike would rejoice and rely on you, the distant would be solemn and the near at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Allow Goguryeo to reform, burn the fleet at Lingbo, and disband the levies—then Chinese and barbarian alike will rejoice, and peace will reach from the frontier to the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣旦夕入地，儻蒙錄此哀鳴，死且不朽！」

translations.literal: Your servant will enter the earth before long; if I may be granted that this piteous cry be recorded, death will yet be imperishable!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall soon be in the grave; if Your Majesty heeds this dying plea, my death will not be in vain."

sentences.zh: 玄齡之遺愛尚上女高陽公主，上謂公主曰：「彼病篤如此，尚能憂我國家。」

translations.literal: Xuanling's beloved wife was married to the emperor's daughter Princess Gaoyang. The emperor told the princess: "Though he is so gravely ill, he can still worry for our state."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling's beloved wife was the emperor's daughter, Princess Gaoyang. The emperor told her, "Though he is this ill, he still worries for the realm."

sentences.zh: 上自臨視，握手與訣，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The emperor himself came to visit, took his hand in farewell, and grief overcame him beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him in person, clasped his hand in farewell, and was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，薨。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, he died.

sentences.zh: 柳芳曰：玄齡佐太宗定天下，及終相位，凡三十二年，天下號為賢相；

translations.literal: Liu Fang said: Xuanling assisted Taizong in settling the realm, and to the end of his chancellorship served thirty-two years in all; the realm called him the worthy chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang wrote: Fang Xuanling helped Taizong secure the realm and served as chancellor for thirty-two years; the world called him the worthy minister;

sentences.zh: 然無跡可尋，德亦至矣。

translations.literal: yet no trace of him can be sought—his virtue had reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: yet he left almost no trace of himself—such was the height of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 故太宗定禍亂而房、杜不言功，王、魏善諫諍而房、杜讓其賢，英、衛善將兵而房、杜行其道，理致太平，善歸人主。

translations.literal: Therefore when Taizong settled turmoil, Fang and Du did not speak of merit; when Wang and Wei were skilled at remonstrance, Fang and Du yielded their worth; when Ying and Wei were skilled at commanding troops, Fang and Du carried out their way. Reason brought the Great Peace, and the good returned to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ended the chaos, Fang and Du did not claim credit; when Wang and Wei excelled at remonstrance, Fang and Du yielded the praise; when Ying and Wei excelled at command, Fang and Du made their policies work. Through such conduct the age reached peace, and the credit went to the throne.

sentences.zh: 為唐宗臣，宜哉！

translations.literal: To be a minister of the Tang house—how fitting!
translations.idiomatic: A minister of the Tang in the truest sense—how fitting!

sentences.zh: 八月，己酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month, day jiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day jiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，敕越州都督府及婺、洪等州造海船及雙舫千一百艘。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, an edict ordered the Yuezhou Protectorate-General and the prefectures of Wu, Hong, and others to build seagoing ships and paired boats—eleven hundred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, the court ordered the Yuezhou protectorate and the prefectures of Wu, Hong, and others to build eleven hundred seagoing ships and paired boats.

sentences.zh: 辛未，遣左領軍大將軍執失思力出金山道擊薛延陀餘寇。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Left Leading Army General Zhishi Sili was sent out by the Jinshan Route to attack remnant bandits of the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, General Zhishi Sili of the Left Leading Army was sent along the Jinshan Route against remnant Xueyantuo raiders.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，昆丘道行軍大總管阿史那社爾擊處月、外密，破之，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gengchen, Campaign Grand Commander of the Kunqiu Route Ashina She'er attacked Chuyue and Waimi, defeated them, and the remaining masses all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day gengchen, Ashina She'er, grand commander of the Kunqiu Route, defeated the Chuyue and Waimi tribes, and all survivors submitted.

sentences.zh: 癸未，薛萬徹等伐高麗還。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Xue Wanche and others returned from campaigning against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Xue Wanche and the others returned from the Goguryeo campaign.

sentences.zh: 萬徹在軍中，使氣陵物，裴行方奏其怨望，坐除名，流象州。

translations.literal: Wanche in the army was overbearing and insulted others. Pei Xingfang memorialized that he harbored resentment; he was punished by removal from the register and exiled to Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the field Wanche had been arrogant and overbearing. Pei Xingfang reported his disaffection; he was stripped of rank and exiled to Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己丑，新羅奏為百濟所攻，破其十三城。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Silla memorialized that it had been attacked by Baekje, which had taken thirteen of its cities.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Silla reported that Baekje had attacked it and captured thirteen cities.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以黃門侍郎褚遂良為中書令。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Yellow Gate Vice Minister Chu Suiliang was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, Chu Suiliang, vice minister of the Yellow Gate, was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 強偉等發民造船，役及山獠，雅、邛、眉三州獠反。

translations.literal: Qiang Wei and others mobilized the people to build ships; the corvée reached the mountain Liao, and the Liao of Ya, Qiong, and Mei prefectures rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Wei and his colleagues conscripted labor for shipbuilding as far as the mountain Liao peoples; the Liao of Ya, Qiong, and Mei prefectures rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遣茂州都督張士貴、右衛將軍梁建方發隴右、峽中兵二萬餘人以擊之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Protector-General Zhang Shigui of Mao Prefecture and Right Guard General Liang Jianfang were sent to mobilize more than twenty thousand troops from Longyou and the gorges to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Zhang Shigui, protector of Mao Prefecture, and Liang Jianfang, general of the Right Guard, were sent with more than twenty thousand troops from Longyou and the gorge region to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 蜀人苦造船之役，或乞輸直雇潭州人造船；

translations.literal: The people of Shu suffered from the shipbuilding corvée; some asked to pay a fee in lieu and hire men of Tan Prefecture to build the ships;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were crushed by shipbuilding labor; some asked to pay a fee instead and have Tan Prefecture build the ships;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 州縣督迫嚴急，民至賣田宅、鬻子女不能供，谷價踴貴，劍外騷然。

translations.literal: The prefectures and districts pressed supervision severely and urgently; the people even sold fields and houses, sold sons and daughters, yet could not meet demands. Grain prices soared; beyond the Sword Pass there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: But local officials drove the work relentlessly. Families sold land and houses, even sold their children, and still could not meet the levies. Grain prices soared, and the region beyond the Sword Pass was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣司農少卿長孫知人馳驛往視之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he sent Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granary Zhangsun Zhiren by post-horse relay to go and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, he sent Zhangsun Zhiren, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Granary, post-haste to investigate.

sentences.zh: 知人奏稱：「蜀人脆弱，不耐勞劇。

translations.literal: Zhiren memorialized, saying: "The people of Shu are frail and cannot endure heavy labor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren reported, "The people of Shu are frail and cannot bear such harsh labor.

sentences.zh: 大船一艘，庸絹二千二百三十六匹。

translations.literal: For one large ship, corvée silk amounts to 2,236 bolts.
translations.idiomatic: A single large ship requires corvée payment of 2,236 bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 山谷已伐之木，挽曳未畢，復征船庸，二事並集，民不能堪，宜加存養。」

translations.literal: Timber already felled in the valleys had not finished being hauled; ship corvée was levied again. The two burdens came together, and the people could not bear it. They should be given added relief and nurture."
translations.idiomatic: Timber already cut in the hills had not yet been hauled out when ship corvée was levied again. The two burdens fell together and the people could not endure them. They need relief."

sentences.zh: 上乃敕潭州船庸皆從官給。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that all ship corvée for Tan Prefecture be supplied from official funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered that shipbuilding costs in Tan Prefecture be paid from government funds.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day guichou, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day guichou, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 回紇吐迷度兄子烏紇蒸其叔母。

translations.literal: Wuna, nephew of the Uyghur Tumedu, committed incest with his uncle's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Wuna, nephew of the Uyghur chief Tumedu, seduced his uncle's wife.

sentences.zh: 烏紇與俱陸莫賀達官俱羅勃，皆突厥車鼻可汗之婿也，相與謀殺吐迷度以歸車鼻。

translations.literal: Wuna and the Julu Mohe dafu Jurubo were both sons-in-law of the Türk qaghan Chebi; together they plotted to kill Tumedu and return to Chebi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuna and Jurubo, a Julu Mohe official, were both sons-in-law of the Türk qaghan Chebi; together they plotted to kill Tumedu and rejoin Chebi.

sentences.zh: 烏紇夜引十餘騎襲吐迷度，殺之。

translations.literal: At night Wuhe led more than ten riders in a raid on Tumidu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wuhe led a dozen horsemen in a surprise attack on Tumidu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 燕然副都護元禮臣使人誘烏紇，許奏以為瀚海都督，烏紇輕騎詣禮臣謝，禮臣執而斬之，以聞。

translations.literal: Assistant Protector-General of Yanran Yuan Lichen sent someone to lure Wuhe, promising to memorialize making him Protector-General of Hanhai; Wuhe came lightly mounted to thank Lichen; Lichen seized and beheaded him and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lichen, deputy protector-general of Yanran, sent agents to entice Wuhe with a promise to recommend him as protector-general of Hanhai. Wuhe rode in lightly to pay his respects; Lichen seized him, executed him, and reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 上恐回紇部落離散，遣兵部尚書崔敦禮往安撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor feared the Uyghur tribes would scatter and sent Minister of War Cui Dunli to go pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Uyghur tribes might disperse, the emperor sent Minister of War Cui Dunli to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 久之，俱羅勃入見，上留之不遣。

translations.literal: After a long time Juluobo came to audience; the emperor kept him and did not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Juluobo came to court; the emperor detained him and would not let him leave.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾既破處月、處密，引兵自焉耆之西趨龜茲北境，分兵為五道，出其不意，焉耆王薛婆阿那支棄城奔龜茲，保其東境。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er, having defeated the Chuyue and Chumi, led troops from west of Yanqi toward the northern border of Kucha, divided the army into five routes, catching them unawares; the King of Yanqi Xuepo Anazhi abandoned the city and fled to Kucha, holding its eastern border.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Chuyue and Chumi, Ashina She'er marched from west of Yanqi toward northern Kucha, split his force into five columns, and struck by surprise. The Yanqi king Xuepo Anazhi abandoned his city and fled to Kucha, where he held the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 社爾遣兵追擊，擒而斬之，立其從父弟先那准為焉耆王，使修職貢。

translations.literal: She'er sent troops in pursuit, captured and beheaded him, installed his younger cousin by the father's side Xiannazhun as King of Yanqi, and had him resume tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: She'er sent pursuers, captured Anazhi, and executed him. He installed the king's younger cousin Xiannazhun as ruler of Yanqi and ordered him to resume tribute.

sentences.zh: 龜茲大震，守將多棄城走。

translations.literal: Kucha was greatly shaken; many garrison commanders abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was thrown into panic, and many garrison commanders abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 社爾進屯磧口，去其都城三百里，遣伊州刺史韓威帥千餘騎為前鋒，驍衛將軍曹繼叔次之。

translations.literal: She'er advanced and encamped at Qikou, three hundred li from their capital; he dispatched Protector-General of Yizhou Han Wei leading more than a thousand horsemen as vanguard, and Valiant Cavalry General Cao Jishu following.
translations.idiomatic: She'er advanced and encamped at Qikou, three hundred li from the Kucha capital. He sent Yizhou protector-general Han Wei ahead with more than a thousand cavalry, followed by valiant cavalry general Cao Jishu.

sentences.zh: 至多褐城，龜茲王訶利布失畢、其相那利、羯獵顛帥眾五萬拒戰。

translations.literal: When they reached Duohuo city, the King of Kucha Helibushibi, his minister Nali, and Jieliedian led fifty thousand to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Duohuo city the Kucha king Helibushibi, his minister Nali, and Jieliedian confronted them with fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 鋒刃甫接，威引兵偽遁，龜茲悉眾追之，行三十里，與繼叔軍合。

translations.literal: As the blades had just met, Wei led troops in feigned retreat; Kucha sent all its forces in pursuit; after thirty li they united with Jishu's army.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the lines clashed, Han Wei feigned retreat. Kucha threw its whole army into the pursuit; thirty li on, his force joined Cao Jishu's.

sentences.zh: 龜茲懼，將卻，繼叔乘之，龜茲大敗，逐北八十里。

translations.literal: Kucha became afraid and was about to withdraw; Jishu pressed them; Kucha was greatly defeated and pursued north eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Kucha army wavered and began to pull back; Jishu pressed the attack and routed them, chasing the fugitives eighty li north.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以回紇吐迷度子翊左郎將婆閏為左驍衛大將軍、大俟利發、瀚海都督。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Tumidu's son, Vice Director of the Left Bodyguard Guards Bolun, was made Senior General of the Left Valiant Guard, Great Yabgu, and Protector-General of Hanhai.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Bolun, son of Tumidu and vice director of the left bodyguard guards, was appointed senior general of the left valiant guard, great yabgu, and protector-general of Hanhai.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚子，契丹帥窟哥、奚帥可度者並帥所部內屬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengzi, the Khitan chieftain Kuge and the Xi chieftain Keduzhe each led their tribes to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day gengzi, the Khitan leader Kuge and the Xi leader Keduzhe each brought their people into Tang allegiance.

sentences.zh: 以契丹部為松漠府，以窟哥為都督；

translations.literal: The Khitan tribe was made Songmo Prefecture, with Kuge as Protector-General;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were organized as Songmo Prefecture, with Kuge as protector-general;

sentences.zh: 又以其別帥達稽等部為峭落等九州，各以其辱紇主為刺史。

translations.literal: and his sub-chiefs Daji and others were made Qiaoluo and the other nine prefectures, each with their Ruohe chiefs as prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: while subordinate leaders such as Daji were formed into Qiaoluo and eight other prefectures, each headed by its own Ruohe chief as prefect.

sentences.zh: 以奚部為饒樂府，以可度者為都督；

translations.literal: The Xi tribe was made Raole Prefecture, with Keduzhe as Protector-General;
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were organized as Raole Prefecture, with Keduzhe as protector-general;

sentences.zh: 又以其別帥阿會等部為弱水等五州，亦各以其辱紇主為刺史。

translations.literal: and his sub-chiefs Ahui and others were made Ruoshui and the other five prefectures, likewise each with their Ruohe chiefs as prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: and subordinates such as Ahui were formed into Ruoshui and four other prefectures, likewise each ruled by a Ruohe chief as prefect.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，置東夷校尉官於營州。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the office of Colonel of the Eastern Tribes was established at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, the post of colonel of the eastern tribes was created at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚午，太子為文德皇后作大慈恩寺成。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, the Crown Prince completed the Great Ci'en Temple built for Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, the crown prince finished the Great Ci'en Temple he had built for Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王布失畢既敗，走保都城，阿史那社爾進軍逼之，布失畢輕騎西走。

translations.literal: The King of Kucha Bushibi, having been defeated, fled to hold the capital city; Ashina She'er advanced the army to press him; Bushibi fled lightly mounted westward.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, the Kucha king Bushibi withdrew into his capital. Ashina She'er pressed the siege, and Bushibi fled westward with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 社爾拔其城，使安西都護郭孝恪守之。

translations.literal: She'er took their city and had Anxi Protector-General Guo Xiaojie hold it.
translations.idiomatic: She'er captured the city and left Anxi protector-general Guo Xiaojie to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 沙州刺史蘇海政、尚輦奉御薛萬備帥精騎追布失畢，行六百里，布失畢窘急，保撥換城，社爾進軍攻之四旬，閏月，丁丑，拔之，擒布失畢及羯獵顛。

translations.literal: Su Haizheng, prefect of Shazhou, and Palace Attendant Xue Wanbei led elite cavalry in pursuit of Bushibi; traveling six hundred li; Bushibi in dire straits held Boluohuan city; She'er advanced to attack for forty days; in the intercalary month, on the day dingchou, took it, capturing Bushibi and Jieliedian.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou prefect Su Haizheng and palace attendant Xue Wanbei pursued Bushibi with elite cavalry for six hundred li. Hard pressed, he held Boluohuan. She'er besieged the place for forty days; in the intercalary month, on the day dingchou, the city fell and Bushibi and Jieliedian were captured.

sentences.zh: 那利脫身走，潛引西突厥之眾並其國兵萬餘人，襲擊孝恪。

translations.literal: Nali escaped alone and fled; secretly led Western Türk forces plus his countrymen of more than ten thousand, raiding Xiaojie.
translations.idiomatic: Nali slipped away alone, secretly rallied more than ten thousand Western Türk allies and Kucha troops, and struck at Guo Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 孝恪營於城外，龜茲人或告之，孝恪不以為意。

translations.literal: Xiaojie camped outside the city; some Kucha men informed him; Xiaojie did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie was encamped outside the walls. Kucha locals warned him, but he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 那利奄至，孝恪帥所部千餘人將入城，那利之眾已登城矣。

translations.literal: Nali arrived suddenly; Xiaojie led his more than thousand men about to enter the city; Nali's forces had already mounted the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Nali struck without warning. Xiaojie mustered his thousand-odd men to re-enter the city, only to find Nali's troops already on the walls.

sentences.zh: 城中降胡與之相應，共擊孝恪，矢刃如雨。

translations.literal: Surrendered barbarians in the city responded to them, jointly attacking Xiaojie; arrows and blades like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered non-Chinese inside the city rose with them and assailed Xiaojie; arrows and blades fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 孝恪不能敵，將復出，死於西門。

translations.literal: Xiaojie could not resist; about to go out again, he died at the West Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie could not hold them off. As he tried to break out again, he was killed at the west gate.

sentences.zh: 城中大擾，倉部郎中崔義超召募得二百人，衛軍資財物，與龜茲戰於城中，曹繼叔、韓威亦營於城外，自城西北隅擊之。

translations.literal: Great disturbance in the city; Warehouse Section Director Cui Yichao recruited two hundred men, guarding military supplies and goods, fighting Kucha in the city; Cao Jishu and Han Wei also encamped outside, attacking from the northwest corner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into chaos. Warehouse section director Cui Yichao raised two hundred men to guard the stores and fought the Kucha forces in the streets. Cao Jishu and Han Wei, camped outside, struck from the northwest corner.

sentences.zh: 那利經宿乃退，斬首三千餘級，城中始定。

translations.literal: Nali after a night then withdrew; beheaded more than three thousand; the city was then stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: After a night of fighting Nali withdrew, leaving more than three thousand dead. Order was restored in the city.

sentences.zh: 後旬餘日，那利復引山北龜茲萬餘人趣都城，繼叔逆擊，大破之，斬首八千級。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Nali again led more than ten thousand Kucha from north of the mountains toward the capital; Jishu met and attacked, greatly defeated them, beheaded eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Some ten days later Nali rallied more than ten thousand Kucha from north of the mountains and marched on the capital. Jishu intercepted them, crushed the force, and took eight thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 那利單騎走，龜茲人執之，以詣軍門。

translations.literal: Nali fled alone on horseback; Kucha men seized him and brought him to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Nali fled alone on horseback. Kucha men seized him and delivered him to the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾前後破其大城五，遣左衛郎將權祗甫詣諸城，開示禍福，皆相帥請降，凡得七百餘城，虜男女數萬口。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er before and after broke five of their great cities; sent Left Guard Captain Quan Zhifu to the various cities, showing fortune and calamity; all led one another in requesting surrender; in all obtained more than seven hundred cities; captured men and women of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er had by then reduced five major cities. He sent left guard captain Quan Zhifu to the outlying towns to proclaim reward and punishment; one after another they submitted, yielding more than seven hundred settlements and tens of thousands of captives.

sentences.zh: 社爾乃召其父老，宣國威靈，諭以伐罪之意，立其王之弟葉護為主，龜茲人大喜。

translations.literal: She'er then summoned their elders, proclaimed national majesty and authority, instructed them on the intent to punish crimes; installed the king's younger brother Yehu as ruler; the people of Kucha were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She'er then assembled the local elders, displayed imperial might, and explained that the campaign was to punish wrongdoing. He installed the former king's younger brother Yehu as ruler, to the great joy of the Kucha people.

sentences.zh: 西域震駭，西突厥、于闐、安國爭饋駝馬軍糧，社爾勒石紀功而還。

translations.literal: The Western Regions were shaken in awe; Western Türks, Khotan, and An Kingdom competed to present camels, horses, and military grain; She'er carved stone to record merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions were stunned. Western Türks, Khotan, and An sent camels, horses, and grain in rivalry; She'er set up a victory stele and marched home.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以昆丘道行軍總管、左驍衛將軍阿史那賀魯為泥伏沙缽羅葉護，賜以鼓纛，使招討西突厥之未服者。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Kunqi Road Campaign Commander-in-Chief and Left Valiant Guard General Ashina Helu was made Nivo Shaboluo Yabghu, granted drums and banners, and sent to recruit and subdue those Western Türks not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin, Kunqi campaign commander and left valiant guard general Ashina Helu was named nivo shaboluo yabghu, given drums and banners, and charged to win over the unsubdued Western Türk tribes.

sentences.zh: 癸未，新羅相金春秋及其子文王入見。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Silla's chancellor Kim Chunchu and his son the Literary King came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Silla's chancellor Kim Chunchu and his son, the Literary King, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 春秋，真德之弟也。

translations.literal: Chunchu was the younger brother of Jinde.
translations.idiomatic: Chunchu was the younger brother of Queen Jinde.

sentences.zh: 上以春秋為特進，文王為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor made Chunchu specially advanced and the Literary King Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Chunchu a specially advanced dignitary and appointed the Literary King general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 春秋請改章服從中國，內出冬服賜之。

translations.literal: Chunchu requested to change dress and insignia to follow China; winter garments were taken from within and bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Chunchu asked to adopt Chinese dress and regalia; the palace issued winter robes from the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，龜茲王布失畢及其相那利等至京師，上責讓而釋之，以布失畢為左武衛中郎將。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, on the day xinhai, the King of Kucha Bushibi and his minister Nali and others arrived at the capital; the emperor rebuked them and released them, making Bushibi Left Martial Guard Vice Captain.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day xinhai, the Kucha king Bushibi, his minister Nali, and others reached the capital. The emperor reproved them but let them go, appointing Bushibi vice captain of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 西南徒莫祗等蠻內附，以其地為傍、望、覽、丘四州，隸朗州都督府。

translations.literal: The southwestern Tumozhi and other barbarians submitted inwardly; their lands were made Bang, Wang, Lan, and Qiu, the four prefectures, subordinate to Langzhou Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Tumozhi and other southwestern tribes submitted. Their territory was divided into the four prefectures of Bang, Wang, Lan, and Qiu under the Langzhou protectorate.

sentences.zh: 上以突厥車鼻可汗不入朝，遣右驍衛郎將高侃發回紇、僕骨等兵襲擊之。

translations.literal: Because the Türk Chieftain Chebi Khan did not come to court, the emperor sent Right Valiant Guard Captain Gao Kan to mobilize Uyghur, Pugu, and other troops to raid attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Türk chieftain Chebi Khan failed to attend court, the emperor sent right valiant guard captain Gao Kan to strike him with Uyghur, Pugu, and allied forces.

sentences.zh: 兵入其境，諸部落相繼來降。

translations.literal: When troops entered their territory, the various tribes came to surrender in succession.
translations.idiomatic: As the army entered his lands, tribe after tribe came over.

sentences.zh: 拔悉密吐屯肥羅察降，以其地置新黎州。

translations.literal: Basmyl chieftain Feiluoqian submitted; their land was made Xinli Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Basmyl chieftain Feiluoqian surrendered, and his territory was organized as Xinli Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，置瑤池都督府，隸安西都護；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day bingxu, established Yaozhi Protectorate, subordinate to Anxi Protector-General;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingxu, the Yaozhi protectorate was created under the Anxi protector-general;

sentences.zh: 戊子，以左衛將軍阿史那賀魯為瑤池都督。

translations.literal: on the day wuzi, made Left Guard General Ashina Helu Yaozhi Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: and on the day wuzi Ashina Helu was named protector-general of Yaozhi.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙辰，置豐州都督府，使燕然都護李素立兼都督。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingchen, established Fengzhou Protectorate, making Yanran Protector-General Li Suli concurrently Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day bingchen, the Fengzhou protectorate was established, with Yanran protector-general Li Suli serving concurrently as its protector-general.

sentences.zh: 去冬旱，至是始雨。

translations.literal: Last winter there was drought; by this time rain finally came.
translations.idiomatic: Drought had persisted since the previous winter; rain finally fell at this time.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上力疾至顯道門外，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, the emperor, forcing himself though ill, went to outside Xiandao Gate and pardoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou, though gravely ill, the emperor forced himself to go outside Xiandao Gate and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，敕太子於金液門聽政。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, ordered the Crown Prince to hear government at Jinye Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, he ordered the crown prince to conduct affairs of state at Jinye Gate.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，上行幸翠微宮。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on the day yihai, the emperor went in progress to Cuiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day yihai, the emperor traveled to Cuiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 上謂太子曰：「李世勣才智有餘，然汝與之無恩，恐不能懷服。

translations.literal: The emperor told the Crown Prince: "Li Shiji has more than enough talent and wisdom, yet you have no grace toward him; I fear he will not embrace and submit in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the crown prince, "Li Shiji is abundantly talented, but you have shown him no favor. I doubt he will serve you willingly.

sentences.zh: 我今黜之，若其即行，俟我死，汝於後用為僕射，親任之；

translations.literal: I now demote him; if he at once goes, wait until I die, then afterward you will use him as Vice Director of the Chancellery and personally entrust affairs to him;
translations.idiomatic: I am demoting him now. If he leaves at once, after I am gone appoint him vice director of the chancellery and rely on him fully.

sentences.zh: 若徘徊顧望，當殺之耳。」

translations.literal: if he hesitates and looks back, you should kill him."
translations.idiomatic: If he hesitates or looks back, have him killed."

sentences.zh: 五月，戊午，以同中書門下三品李世勣為疊州都督；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day wuwu, made Fellow-Chancellor-with-the-Secretariat Li Shiji Protector-General of Diezhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wuwu, fellow chancellor Li Shiji was made protector-general of Diezhou;

sentences.zh: 世勣受詔，不至家而去。

translations.literal: Shiji received the edict and, without going home, departed.
translations.idiomatic: and Shiji, on receiving the order, left at once without even stopping at home.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，開府儀同三司衛景武公李靖薨。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Grand Master of Glorious Magnanimity and Concurrent Honor for the Three Duties Duke of Weijing the Martial, Li Jing, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou, Li Jing, Duke of Weijing the Martial and grand master of glorious magnanimity with concurrent honor for the three duties, died.

sentences.zh: 上苦利增劇，太子晝夜不離側，或累日不食，發有變白者。

translations.literal: The emperor's diarrhea grew severely worse; the Crown Prince day and night did not leave his side; sometimes for many days did not eat; hair appeared that had turned white.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's dysentery worsened sharply. The crown prince never left his bedside, sometimes going days without food; strands of his hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 上泣曰：「汝能孝愛如此，吾死何恨！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "You can be so filially loving—what regret have I in death!
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the emperor said, "Such devotion—what regret can I have in dying!

sentences.zh: 丁卯，疾篤，召長孫無忌入含風殿。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, illness critical, summoned Zhangsun Wuji into Hanfeng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, as his illness turned critical, he summoned Zhangsun Wuji to Hanfeng Hall.

sentences.zh: 上臥，引手捫無忌頤，無忌哭，悲不自勝；

translations.literal: The emperor lay down and reached out his hand to stroke Wuji's cheek; Wuji wept, grief beyond bearing himself;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lay back and touched Wuji's cheek; Wuji wept until he could no longer contain himself;

sentences.zh: 上竟不得有所言，因令無忌出。

translations.literal: the emperor in the end could not say anything and therefore ordered Wuji out.
translations.idiomatic: but the emperor could not speak after all and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 己巳，復召無忌及褚遂良入臥內，謂之曰：「朕今悉以後事付公輩。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, again summoned Wuji and Chu Suiliang into the sleeping quarters and told them: "I now entirely entrust later affairs to you all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi he again called Wuji and Chu Suiliang to his bedside and said, "I now entrust everything that follows to you.

sentences.zh: 太子仁孝，公輩所知，善輔導之！」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince is benevolent and filial, as you all know—well guide and assist him!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is benevolent and filial, as you know. Guide him well!

sentences.zh: 謂太子曰：「無忌、遂良在，汝勿憂天下！」

translations.literal: He told the Crown Prince: "With Wuji and Suiliang present, you need not worry over the realm!
translations.idiomatic: He told the crown prince, "With Wuji and Suiliang at your side, you need not fear for the realm!

sentences.zh: 又謂遂良曰：「無忌盡忠於我，我有天下，多其力也。

translations.literal: He also told Suiliang: "Wuji is utterly loyal to me; in gaining the realm I had much of his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Suiliang, "Wuji has been utterly loyal to me. I owe much of my throne to him.

sentences.zh: 我死，勿令讒人間之。」

translations.literal: When I die, do not let slanderers come between us.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, do not let anyone drive a wedge between you.

sentences.zh: 仍令遂良草遺詔。

translations.literal: He still ordered Suiliang to draft the final edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Suiliang to draft the final edict.

sentences.zh: 有頃，上崩。

translations.literal: Before long, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 太子擁無忌頸，號慟將絕。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince embraced Wuji's neck, wailing until nearly fainting.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince clung to Wuji's neck and wailed until he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 無忌攬涕，請處分眾事以安內外。

translations.literal: Wuji wiped tears and requested to handle the multitude of affairs to settle inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji dried his tears and urged that state affairs be settled to calm court and country.

sentences.zh: 太子哀號不已，無忌曰：「主上以宗廟社稷付殿下，豈得效匹夫唯哭泣乎！」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince mourned unceasingly; Wuji said: "The late sovereign entrusted the altars and state to Your Highness—how can you act like a common fellow and only weep!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince would not stop grieving. Wuji said, "The late emperor entrusted the altars of state to you—will you behave like a common mourner and do nothing but weep!

sentences.zh: 乃秘不發喪。

translations.literal: They therefore kept the death secret and did not announce it.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore concealed the death and made no public announcement.

sentences.zh: 庚午，無忌等請太子先還，飛騎、勁兵及舊將皆從。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Wuji and others requested the Crown Prince return first; flying cavalry, crack troops, and old generals all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, Wuji and the others urged the crown prince to go back first; flying cavalry, picked troops, and veteran commanders all accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，太子入京城；

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the Crown Prince entered the capital city;
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei the crown prince entered the capital;

sentences.zh: 大行御馬輿，侍衛如平日，繼太子而至，頓於兩儀殿。

translations.literal: the late emperor's imperial horse carriage, attendants as on ordinary days, followed after the Crown Prince and halted at Liangyi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: the late emperor's imperial carriage, with attendants as on an ordinary day, followed behind and halted at Liangyi Hall.

sentences.zh: 以太子左庶子於志寧為侍中，少詹事張行成兼侍中，以檢校刑部尚書、右庶子、兼吏部侍郎高季輔兼中書令。

translations.literal: Made the Crown Prince's Left Palace Director Yu Zhining Attendant-in-Chief, Junior Chamberlain Zhang Xingcheng Concurrently Attendant-in-Chief, and Inspection Commissioner of the Ministry of Justice, Right Palace Director, and Concurrent Vice Director of Personnel Gao Jifu Concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining, left palace director to the crown prince, was made attendant-in-chief; junior chamberlain Zhang Xingcheng was made concurrent attendant-in-chief; and Gao Jifu, inspection commissioner of the ministry of justice, right palace director, and concurrent vice director of personnel, was made concurrent director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬申，發喪太極殿，宣遺詔，太子即位。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, announced mourning at Taiji Hall, proclaimed the final edict; the Crown Prince ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen mourning was proclaimed in Taiji Hall, the final edict was read, and the crown prince ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 軍國大事，不可停闕；

translations.literal: Military and state great affairs may not be halted or lacking;
translations.idiomatic: Urgent matters of war and state must not be neglected;

sentences.zh: 平常細務，委之有司。

translations.literal: ordinary minor affairs are entrusted to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: routine business is left to the proper ministries.

sentences.zh: 諸王為都督、刺史者，並聽奔喪，濮王泰不在來限。

translations.literal: Princes who are Protectors-General or prefectural governors are all permitted to hurry to mourning; Prince of Pu Li Tai is not within those who may come.
translations.idiomatic: Princes serving as protector-generals or prefects may all return for the funeral; Prince of Pu Li Tai is excluded.

sentences.zh: 罷遼東之役及諸土木之功。

translations.literal: Abolished the Liaodong campaign and various earthen and wooden works.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong expedition and various earth-and-timber projects were canceled.

sentences.zh: 四夷之人入仕於朝及來朝貢者數百人，聞喪皆慟哭，剪髮、剺面、割耳，流血灑地。

translations.literal: Several hundred men from the four barbarians entering office at court and coming to pay tribute, hearing of the death all wailed in grief, cut hair, lacerated face, cut ears, blood spilling on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred foreign envoys and officials at court, hearing the news, wailed in grief, cut their hair, slashed their faces, even cut off their ears, until blood soaked the ground.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌朔，高宗即位，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month jiaxu, Gaozong ascended the throne and pardoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day jiaxu, Gaozong took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以疊州都督李勣為特進、檢校洛州刺史、洛陽宮留守。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, made Diezhou Protector-General Li Jing specially advanced, inspection commissioner of Luozhou and Luoyang Palace garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Diezhou protector-general Li Jing was made specially advanced, inspection commissioner of Luozhou, and garrison commander of Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗二名，令天下不連言者勿避；

translations.literal: Previously, Taizong had two names; he ordered that throughout the realm those who did not speak them in continuous speech need not avoid them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Taizong had borne two personal names and ruled that the realm need not avoid them unless they were spoken together as his full name;

sentences.zh: 至是，始改官名犯先帝諱者。

translations.literal: by this time they first changed official names that violated the late emperor's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: now, for the first time, official titles that clashed with the late emperor's taboo were renamed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以長孫無忌為太尉，兼檢校中書令，知尚書、門下二省事。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, made Zhangsun Wuji Grand Preceptor, concurrently inspection commissioner of the Secretariat, knowing the affairs of the Ministries of State and of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Zhangsun Wuji was appointed grand preceptor, concurrent inspection commissioner of the secretariat, with charge of the ministries of state and of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 無忌固辭知尚書省事，帝許之，仍令以大尉同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Wuji firmly declined knowing Secretariat affairs; the emperor permitted it, still ordering that as Grand Preceptor he be Fellow-Chancellor-with-the-Secretariat at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji firmly declined day-to-day secretariat duties; the new emperor agreed but kept him as grand preceptor and fellow chancellor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以李勣為開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, made Li Jing Grand Master of Glorious Magnanimity with Credential, Fellow-Chancellor-with-the-Secretariat at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Li Jing was made grand master of glorious magnanimity with credential and fellow chancellor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾之破龜茲也，行軍長史薛萬備請因兵威說于闐王伏闍信入朝，社爾從之。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er destroyed Kucha, Campaign Chief of Staff Xue Wanbei requested using military prestige to persuade the King of Khotan Fuxinxin to enter court; She'er followed this.
translations.idiomatic: After Ashina She'er conquered Kucha, campaign chief of staff Xue Wanbei urged using the army's prestige to bring the Khotan king Fuxinxin to court, and She'er agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉，伏闍信隨萬備入朝，詔入謁梓宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, on the day jiyou, Fuxinxin followed Wanbei to enter court; an edict ordered him to pay respects at the late emperor's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jiyou, Fuxinxin accompanied Wanbei to the capital; an edict directed him to pay homage before the late emperor's coffin.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸酉，夜，地震，晉州尤甚，壓殺五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day guiyou, at night, earthquake; Jin Prefecture especially severe; crushed and killed more than five thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day guiyou, an earthquake struck at night. Jin Prefecture suffered worst, with more than five thousand people crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，葬文皇帝於昭陵，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, buried the Literary Emperor at Zhaoling; temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, the Literary Emperor was buried at Zhaoling; his temple name was Taizong.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾、契苾何力請殺身殉葬，上遣人諭以先旨不許。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er and Qibi Heli requested to kill themselves to follow in burial; the emperor sent someone to instruct them that the late sovereign's prior intent did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er and Qibi Heli asked to die and follow him into the tomb; the emperor sent word that the late sovereign's earlier command forbade it.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷君長為先帝所擒服者頡利等十四人，皆琢石為其像，刻名列於北司馬門內。

translations.literal: Barbarian chieftains and lords whom the late emperor had captured and subdued—Jieli and fourteen others—all had stone carved as their images, names carved and listed within the north Gate of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen barbarian rulers whom the late emperor had subdued, including Jieli, were carved in stone and their names inscribed inside the north gate of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，禮部尚書許敬宗奏弘農府君廟應毀，請藏主於西夾室；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong memorialized that the Hongnong Prince Grandfather temple should be destroyed, requesting to store the spirit tablets in the western side chamber;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong memorialized that the Hongnong Prince Grandfather shrine should be demolished and the spirit tablets moved to the western side chamber;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: the court approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，以李勣為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day yimao, made Li Jing Left Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day yimao, Li Jing was appointed left vice director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以突厥諸部置捨利等五州隸雲中都督府，蘇農等六州隸定襄都督府。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, placed Türk various tribes in Sheli and the other five prefectures subordinate to Yunzhong Protectorate, Su'nong and the other six subordinate to Dingxiang Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Türk tribes were organized into Sheli and four other prefectures under Yunzhong protectorate, and Su'nong and five others under Dingxiang protectorate.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上問大理卿唐臨系囚之數，對曰：「見囚五十餘人，唯二人應死。」

translations.literal: On yihai, the emperor asked Minister of Justice Tang Lin the number of prisoners in custody; he replied: "Of prisoners now held, more than fifty; only two deserve death."
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, the emperor asked Tang Lin, minister of justice, how many prisoners were held; he answered that of more than fifty detainees, only two merited execution.

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 上嘗錄系囚，前卿所處者多號呼稱冤，臨所處者獨無言。

translations.literal: The emperor once reviewed prisoners in custody; those judged by the previous minister mostly shouted claiming injustice, while those Tang Lin had judged alone were silent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor once reviewed prisoners, those handled by the previous minister cried out that they had been wronged, but those Tang Lin had judged remained silent.

sentences.zh: 上怪，問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered at this and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was puzzled and asked why.

sentences.zh: 囚曰：「唐卿所處，本自無冤。」

translations.literal: A prisoner said: "What Minister Tang judged had no injustice from the start."
translations.idiomatic: A prisoner said, "Minister Tang's rulings were never unjust in the first place."

sentences.zh: 上歎息良久，曰：「治獄者不當如是邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed long and said: "Should those who judge prisons not be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed for a long while and said, "Ought not every judge of prisoners be like this!"

sentences.zh: 上以吐蕃贊普弄贊為駙馬都尉，封西海郡王。

translations.literal: The emperor made the Tibetan tsanpo Songtsän Gampo Imperial Son-in-law Commandant and enfeoffed him as King of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed the Tibetan tsanpo Songtsän Gampo imperial son-in-law commandant and enfeoffed him as king of Xihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 贊普致書於長孫無忌等云：「天子初即位，臣下有不忠者，當勒兵赴國討除之。」

translations.literal: The tsanpo sent a letter to Zhangsun Wuji and others saying: "The Son of Heaven has just ascended the throne; if any among your subjects is disloyal, I shall lead troops to the state to strike and eliminate them."
translations.idiomatic: The tsanpo wrote to Zhangsun Wuji and others: "Now that the Son of Heaven has newly taken the throne, if any subject proves disloyal, I shall muster troops and come to the realm to punish and remove him."
translations.footnote: The letter's quoted passage ends here

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔濮王泰開府置僚屬，車服珍膳，特加優異。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered Prince of Pu Li Tai to open a mansion and appoint staff; carriages, robes, and fine foods were granted with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict directed Prince of Pu Li Tai to establish a princely establishment with staff; his carriage regalia and fine provisions were singled out for exceptional treatment.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大聖大弘孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign, Great Sage, Great Extender of Filial Piety — Upper, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong the Heavenly Sovereign, Great Sage, and Great Extender of Filial Piety — Upper, Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑朔，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinchou the new moon, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the cyclical day xinchou, a new reign title was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丙午，立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the consort née Wang was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu, Lady Wang was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 后，思政之孫也。

translations.literal: The empress was a granddaughter of Wang Si'en.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a granddaughter of Wang Si'en.

sentences.zh: 以后父仁祐為特進、魏國公。

translations.literal: The empress's father Wang Renyou was made Special Advancement-holder and Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang Renyou was appointed special advancement-holder and duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 己未，以張行成為侍中。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Zhang Xingcheng was made Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Zhang Xingcheng was made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上召朝集使，謂曰：「朕初即位，事有不便於百姓者悉宜陳，不盡者更封奏。」

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor summoned the assembly envoys and said: "I have just ascended the throne; whatever is not convenient for the common people you should all state; what you do not fully state, submit again in sealed memorial."
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou, the emperor summoned the provincial assembly envoys and said, "I have only lately taken the throne. Whatever harms the people should be reported fully; anything left unsaid may be submitted later in a sealed memorial."

sentences.zh: 自是日引刺史十人入閣，問以百姓疾苦，及其政治。

translations.literal: From then on, each day he brought in ten prefects to the inner hall and questioned them on the people's hardships and their governance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he daily summoned ten prefects into the inner hall to inquire about popular hardship and the quality of their administration.

sentences.zh: 有洛陽人李弘泰誣告長孫無忌謀反，上立命斬之。

translations.literal: A man of Luoyang, Li Hongtai, falsely accused Zhangsun Wuji of plotting rebellion; the emperor immediately ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongtai of Luoyang falsely charged Zhangsun Wuji with treason, and the emperor at once ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 無忌與褚遂良同心輔政，上亦尊禮二人，恭己以聽之，故永徽之政，百姓阜安，有貞觀之遺風。

translations.literal: Wuji and Chu Suiliang with one mind assisted in government; the emperor also honored the two men and with a deferential posture listened to them — thus under Yonghui the people were secure and prosperous, with the legacy spirit of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Chu Suiliang governed in concert; the emperor honored both and yielded to their counsel. Under the Yonghui reign the people flourished in peace, and the governance still bore the spirit of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 太宗女衡山公主應適長孫氏，有司以為服既公除，欲以今秋成昏。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong's daughter Princess Hengshan was to marry into the Zhangsun clan; the relevant offices held that mourning had reached the end of the public mourning period and wished to complete the marriage this autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Hengshan, a daughter of Emperor Taizong, was to marry a member of the Zhangsun house; the responsible offices held that public mourning had ended and proposed holding the wedding that autumn.

sentences.zh: 於志寧上言：「漢文立制，本為天下百姓。

translations.literal: Yu Zhining memorialized: "When Emperor Wen of Han established institutions, it was fundamentally for the common people under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining memorialized: "When Emperor Wen of Han framed his institutions, he did so for the sake of the people under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 公主服本斬衰，縱使服隨例除，豈可情隨例改，請俟三年喪畢成昏。」

translations.literal: The princess's mourning is the severest grade; even if mourning follows precedent in being removed, how can feeling follow precedent in changing? I request waiting until the three-year mourning is finished to complete the marriage."
translations.idiomatic: The princess wears the severest mourning; even if mourning may be cut short by precedent, affection cannot be altered by precedent. I ask that the marriage wait until the three-year mourning is complete."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，立皇子孝為許王，上金為杞王，素節為雍王。

translations.literal: Second month, xinmao, established princes Xiao as King of Xu, Shangjin as King of Qi, and Su Jie as King of Yong.
