translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day xinmao, Prince Xiao was made king of Xu, Prince Shangjin king of Qi, and Prince Su Jie king of Yong.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬戌，吐蕃贊普弄贊卒，其嫡子早死，立其孫為贊普。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, renxu, the Tibetan tsanpo Songtsän Gampo died; his legitimate son had died early, and they established his grandson as tsanpo.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day renxu, the Tibetan tsanpo Songtsän Gampo died; his heir had died young, so his grandson was enthroned as tsanpo.

sentences.zh: 贊普幼弱，政事皆決於國相祿東贊。

translations.literal: The tsanpo was young and weak; all government affairs were decided by the state chancellor Gar Tongtsen.
translations.idiomatic: The tsanpo was still a child, and all state affairs were decided by the chief minister Gar Tongtsen.

sentences.zh: 祿東贊性明達嚴重，行兵有法，吐蕃所以強大，威服氐、羌，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: Gar Tongtsen was by nature perspicacious, severe, and dignified; in campaigning he had method — Tibet's strength and subjugation of Di and Qiang were all through his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen was clear-sighted, stern, and grave, and disciplined in warfare; Tibet's rise to power and its subjugation of the Di and Qiang were largely his doing.

sentences.zh: 六月，高侃擊突厥，至阿息山。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Gao Kan attacked the Turks and reached Mount Axi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Gao Kan attacked the Turks and advanced to Mount Axi.

sentences.zh: 車鼻可汗召諸部兵皆不赴，與數百騎遁去。

translations.literal: Chebi Khan summoned the troops of all tribes but none came; with several hundred horsemen he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi Khan called up the tribal armies, but none answered; he fled with only a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 侃帥精騎追至金山，擒之以歸，其眾皆降。

translations.literal: Kan led elite cavalry in pursuit to Jinshan, captured him and brought him back; all his followers submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kan pursued with picked cavalry to Jinshan, seized him, and brought him back; his entire following surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，阿史那社爾虜龜茲王布失畢，立其弟為王。

translations.literal: Initially, Ashina She'er captured the Kucha king Bu Shibi and installed his younger brother as king.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ashina She'er had captured the Kucha king Bu Shibi and set up the king's younger brother in his place.

sentences.zh: 唐兵既還，其酋長爭立，更相攻擊。

translations.literal: After Tang troops had returned, the chieftains vied to install themselves and attacked one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang army withdrew, the tribal leaders fought one another in succession for the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬午，詔復以布失畢為龜茲王，遣歸國，撫其眾。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, renwu, an edict restored Bu Shibi as king of Kucha, sent him back to his state, and pacified his people.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day renwu, an edict restored Bu Shibi as king of Kucha, sent him home, and charged him to reassure his people.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚子，高侃執車鼻可汗至京師，釋之，拜左武衛將軍，處其餘眾於郁督軍山，置狼山都督府以統之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, gengzi, Gao Kan brought Chebi Khan to the capital, released him, appointed him General of the Left Martial Guards, placed his remaining followers at Yudujun Mountain, and established the Langshan Area Command to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day gengzi, Gao Kan delivered Chebi Khan to the capital; the emperor released him, made him general of the left martial guards, settled his remaining followers at Yudujun Mountain, and created the Langshan area command to govern them.

sentences.zh: 以高侃為衛將軍。

translations.literal: Gao Kan was made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan was appointed general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥盡為封內之臣，分置單于、瀚海二都護府。

translations.literal: Thereupon all Turks became subjects within the borders; the Chanyu and Hanhai two Protectorates were separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Turks were wholly subjects within the frontier, and the Chanyu and Hanhai protectorates were set up separately.

sentences.zh: 單于領狼山、雲中、桑干三都督，蘇農等一十四州；

translations.literal: Chanyu oversaw Langshan, Yunzhong, and Sanggan three area commands and fourteen prefectures including Sunong.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu protectorate governed three area commands—Langshan, Yunzhong, and Sanggan—and fourteen prefectures including Sunong.

sentences.zh: 瀚海領瀚海、金徽、新黎等七都督，仙萼等八州；

translations.literal: Hanhai oversaw seven area commands including Hanhai, Jinwei, and Xinli, and eight prefectures including Xian'e;
translations.idiomatic: The Hanhai protectorate governed seven area commands, among them Hanhai, Jinwei, and Xinli, and eight prefectures including Xian'e;

sentences.zh: 各以其酋長為都督、刺史。

translations.literal: In each case their chieftains served as area commanders and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the tribal chiefs were appointed area commanders and prefects.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上出畋，遇雨，問諫議大夫昌樂谷那律曰：「油衣若為則不漏？」

translations.literal: On guihai, the emperor went out hunting, encountered rain, and asked Remonstrating Censor Gu Nile of Changle Valley: "How would an oil garment be made so it does not leak?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, the emperor went hunting, was caught in rain, and asked Remonstrating Censor Gu Nile of Changle Valley, "How might an oilskin cloak be made so that it does not leak?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以瓦為之，必不漏。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If made of tile, it would certainly not leak."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If it were made of tile, it would surely not leak."

sentences.zh: 上悅，為之罷獵。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and for this sake ended the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and called off the hunt on that account.

sentences.zh: 李勣固求解職；

translations.literal: Li Ji firmly requested to resign his post;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji repeatedly asked to resign his office;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊辰，解勣左僕射，以開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, wuchen, relieved Ji of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, making him Honorary Grand Master with Golden Seal and Ribbon, co-equal with the Secretariat-Chancellery at Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day wuchen, he was relieved of the left vice directorship of the Department of State Affairs and made honorary grand master with golden seal and ribbon, co-equal with the secretariat-chancellery at third rank.

sentences.zh: 己未，監察御史陽武韋思謙劾奏中書令褚遂良抑買中書譯語人地。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Supervising Censor Wei Siqian of Yangwu impeached Secretariat Director Chu Suiliang for forcibly buying land belonging to the Secretariat translator-interpreter.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Supervising Censor Wei Siqian of Yangwu impeached Secretariat Director Chu Suiliang for coercively purchasing land held by a secretariat interpreter.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿張睿冊以為準估無罪。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of Justice Zhang Ruice held that under the standard valuation there was no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant director of justice Zhang Ruice ruled that, measured against the standard valuation, there was no offense.

sentences.zh: 思謙奏曰：「估價之設，備國家所須，臣下交易，豈得准估為定！

translations.literal: Siqian memorialized: "The establishing of valuation prices exists to supply what the state needs; when subordinates trade, how can the standard valuation be taken as fixed!
translations.idiomatic: Siqian memorialized: "Valuation prices exist for the state's needs; when officials trade among themselves, how can the standard price be treated as binding!

sentences.zh: 睿冊舞文，附下罔上，罪當誅。」

translations.literal: Ruice twists the text of law, attaches himself to those below to deceive those above — the crime deserves execution."
translations.idiomatic: Ruice twists the statutes, siding with inferiors to mislead superiors—the offense deserves death."

sentences.zh: 是日，左遷遂良為同刺史，睿冊循州刺史。

translations.literal: That day, Chu Suiliang was demoted to prefect of Tong and Ruice to prefect of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Chu Suiliang was demoted to prefect of Tong and Zhang Ruice to prefect of Xun.

sentences.zh: 思謙名仁約，以字行。

translations.literal: Siqian's name was Renyue; he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian's personal name was Renyue; he was commonly known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚午，梓州都督謝萬歲、兗州都督謝法興與黔州都督李孟嘗討琰州叛獠；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, gengwu, Zizhou Area Commander Xie Wansui, Yanzhou Area Commander Xie Faxing, and Qianzhou Area Commander Li Mengchang attacked the rebellious liao of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengwu, Zizhou area commander Xie Wansui, Yanzhou area commander Xie Faxing, and Qianzhou area commander Li Mengchang campaigned against rebellious liao in Yan prefecture;

sentences.zh: 萬歲、法興入洞招慰，為獠所殺。

translations.literal: Wansui and Faxing entered caves to summon and comfort them and were killed by the liao.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui and Faxing entered the caves to offer reassurance and were slain by the liao.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳，以黃門侍郎宇文節、中書侍郎柳奭並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, yisi, made Yellow Gate Attendant Yu Wenjie and Secretariat Attendant Liu Shi both co-equal with Secretariat-Chancellery at Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day yisi, Yellow Gate Attendant Yu Wenjie and Secretariat Attendant Liu Shi were both made co-equal with the secretariat-chancellery at third rank.

sentences.zh: 奭，亨之兄子，王皇后之舅也。

translations.literal: Shi was a nephew of Liu Xing's son; he was Empress Wang's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi was a nephew of Liu Xing's lineage and the empress's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 左驍衛將軍、瑤池都督阿史那賀魯招集離散，廬帳漸盛，聞太宗崩，謀襲取西、庭二州。

translations.literal: Left Swift Tiger General and Protector of Yaochi Ashina Helu gathered the scattered and his tents gradually flourished; hearing Taizong had died, he plotted to seize Xi and Ting prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Left Swift Tiger General and Protector of Yaochi Ashina Helu rallied the dispersed tribes until his encampments grew strong; when he heard that Taizong had died, he plotted to seize the Xi and Ting protectorates.

sentences.zh: 庭州刺史駱弘義知其謀，表言之，上遣通事舍人橋寶明馳往慰撫。

translations.literal: Tingzhou prefect Luo Hongyi knew his plot, memorialized it; the emperor sent Imperial Diarist Qiao Baoming post-haste to console and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhou prefect Luo Hongyi learned of the plot and reported it; the emperor sent imperial diarist Qiao Baoming post-haste to console and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 寶明說賀魯，令長子咥運入宿衛，授右驍衛中郎將，尋復遣歸。

translations.literal: Baoming persuaded Helu to send his eldest son Nishu to enter palace guard service; he was appointed Middle General of the Right Swift Tiger Guards, then soon sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Baoming persuaded Helu to send his eldest son Nishu to serve in the palace guard; Nishu was made middle general of the right swift tiger guards, then soon sent home again.

sentences.zh: 咥運乃說其父擁眾西走，擊破乙毘射匱可汗，並其眾，建牙於雙河及千泉，自號沙缽羅可汗，咄陸五啜、努失畢五俟斤皆歸之，勝兵數十萬，與乙毘咄陸可汗連兵，處月、處密及西域諸國多附之。

translations.literal: Nishu then persuaded his father to lead his followers west; they defeated the Yibilishi Kaghan, absorbed his followers, established a royal encampment at Shuanghe and Qianquan, styled himself Shaboluo Kaghan; the five chuo of the Zhuolu and the five irkin of the Nushibi all submitted to him; battle-ready troops numbered hundreds of thousands; he allied with the Yibizhuolu Kaghan; the Chuyue, Chumi, and many states of the Western Regions largely attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Nishu then urged his father to march west with a great following, defeated the Yibilishi kaghan, and absorbed his people; Helu set up his headquarters at Shuanghe and Qianquan and styled himself Shaboluo kaghan. The five chuo of the Zhuolu and the five irkin of the Nushibi all joined him, and his field army reached several hundred thousand. Allied with the Yibizhuolu kaghan, he drew the Chuyue, Chumi, and many Western Region states to his side.

sentences.zh: 以咥運為莫賀咄葉護。

translations.literal: Nishu was made Mohe Duduye Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Nishu was appointed Mohe Duduye Protector.

sentences.zh: 焉耆王婆伽利卒，國人表請復立故王突騎支；

translations.literal: King of Yanqi Bogali died; the people petitioned to restore the former king Tuqizhi;
translations.idiomatic: The king of Yanqi, Bogali, died, and the people petitioned to restore the former king Tuqizhi;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，詔加突騎支右武衛將軍，遣還國。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, edict promoted Tuqizhi to General of the Right Martial Guards and sent him back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, an edict made Tuqizhi general of the right martial guards and sent him back to his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 金州刺史滕王元嬰驕奢縱逸，居亮陰中，畋游無節，數夜開城門，勞擾百姓，或引彈彈人，或埋人雪中以戲笑。

translations.literal: Prince Teng Li Yuanying at Jinzhou was arrogant and extravagant, unrestrained in mourning residence, hunting without limit, repeatedly opening the city gate at night and troubling the people, sometimes setting up catapults to launch men, sometimes burying men in snow for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou, Prince Teng Li Yuanying was arrogant and dissolute; even while observing mourning for the late emperor he hunted without restraint, often opened the city gates at night to disturb the people, and amused himself by launching men with catapults or burying them in snow.

sentences.zh: 上賜書切讓之，且曰：「取適之方，亦應多緒，晉靈荒君，何足為則！

translations.literal: The emperor sent a letter sternly reproving him, and also said: "Methods of seeking pleasure should be many and varied; Duke Ling of Jin the wastrel lord — how is he fit to be taken as a model!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a stern letter of rebuke, adding, "There are many proper ways to find diversion; Duke Ling of Jin in his debauchery is hardly a model to follow!

sentences.zh: 朕以王至親，不能致王於法，今書王下上考以愧王心。」

translations.literal: I, considering the prince's closest kinship, cannot bring the prince under the law; now I record for the prince the next-to-lowest grade to shame the prince's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Because you are my close kinsman I cannot subject you to the law; I therefore mark you with the next-to-lowest performance grade to stir your conscience."

sentences.zh: 元嬰與蔣王惲皆好聚斂，上嘗賜諸王帛各五百段，獨不及二王，敕曰：「滕叔、蔣兄自能經紀，不須賜物；

translations.literal: Yuanying and Prince Jiang both loved amassing wealth; when the emperor once gave each prince five hundred bolts of silk, he alone omitted the two princes, edict saying: "Uncle Teng and Brother Jiang can manage for themselves and need no gifts;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying and Prince Jiang were both avid for gain; when the emperor once granted every prince five hundred bolts of silk, he alone excluded the two, decreeing, "Uncle Teng and Brother Jiang can look after themselves and need no gifts;

sentences.zh: 給麻兩車以為錢貫。」

translations.literal: give two cartloads of hemp as coin strings."
translations.idiomatic: give them two cartloads of hemp to serve as money strings."

sentences.zh: 二王大慚。

translations.literal: The two princes were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，西突厥沙缽羅可汗寇庭州，攻陷金嶺城及蒲類縣，殺略數千人。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Western Türk Shaboluo Kaghan raided Tingzhou, captured Jincheng and Pulei counties, and killed and plundered several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Western Türk Shaboluo kaghan attacked Tingzhou, took Jincheng and Pulei counties, and killed or carried off several thousand people.

sentences.zh: 詔左武候大將軍梁建方、右驍衛大將軍契苾何力為弓月道行軍總管，右驍衛將軍高德逸、右武候將軍薛孤吳仁為副，發秦、成、岐、雍府兵三萬人及回紇五萬騎以討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Left Martial Guards General Liang Jianfang and Right Swift Tiger Guards General Qibi Heli campaign generals of the Gongyue Circuit, with Right Swift Tiger Guards General Gao Deyi and Right Martial Guards General Xue Gu Wuren as deputies, mobilizing thirty thousand troops from the Qin, Cheng, Qi, and Yong prefectural armies and fifty thousand Uyghur horsemen to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Left Martial Guards General Liang Jianfang and Right Swift Tiger Guards General Qibi Heli as campaign generals of the Gongyue circuit, with Right Swift Tiger Guards General Gao Deyi and Right Martial Guards General Xue Gu Wuren as deputies, and sent thirty thousand men from the Qin, Cheng, Qi, and Yong prefectural armies plus fifty thousand Uyghur cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔諸禮官學士議明堂制度，以高祖配五天帝，太宗配五人帝。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict ordered ritual officials and academicians to discuss the Hall of Enlightened Rule system, pairing Gaozu with the Five Heavenly Emperors and Taizong with the Five Human Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, an edict directed ritual officials and scholars to debate the Hall of Enlightened Rule, assigning Gaozu to the Five Heavenly Emperors and Taizong to the Five Human Emperors.

sentences.zh: 八月，己巳，以於志寧為左僕射，張行成為右僕射，高季輔為侍中；

translations.literal: Eighth month, jisi, made Yu Zhining Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Zhang Xingcheng Right Vice Director, and Gao Jifu Attendant-in-ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jisi, Yu Zhining was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, Zhang Xingcheng right vice director, and Gao Jifu attendant-in-ordinary;

sentences.zh: 志寧、行成仍同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Zhining and Xingcheng remained co-equal with Secretariat-Chancellery at Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining and Xingcheng continued as co-equal with the secretariat-chancellery at third rank.

sentences.zh: 己卯，郎州白水蠻反，寇麻州，遣左領軍將軍趙孝祖等發兵討之。

translations.literal: On jimao, the Baishui barbarians of Langzhou rebelled and raided Ma prefecture; Left Leading General Zhao Xiaozu and others were sent with troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, the Baishui barbarians of Langzhou rose in revolt and raided Ma prefecture; the court dispatched Left Leading General Zhao Xiaozu and others to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，廢玉華宮為佛寺。

translations.literal: Ninth month, guisi, the Yuhua Palace was abolished and made a Buddhist monastery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day guisi, Yuhua Palace was converted into a Buddhist monastery.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，更命九成宮為萬年宮。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Jiucheng Palace was renamed Wannian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Jiucheng Palace was renamed Wannian Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，左武候引駕盧文操逾牆盜左藏物，上以引駕職在糾繩，乃自為盜，命誅之。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Left Martial Guards Lead Escort Lu Wencao climbed the wall and stole goods from the left treasury; because the lead escort's duty is to restrain wrongdoing, yet he himself became a thief, the emperor ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Left Martial Guards lead escort Lu Wencao scaled the wall and stole from the left treasury; since his post was to enforce discipline yet he had turned thief himself, the emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫蕭鈞諫曰：「文操情實難原，然法不至死。」

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Xiao Jun remonstrated: "Wencao's circumstances are hard to pardon, yet the law does not reach death."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Xiao Jun argued: "Wencao's offense is grave, yet the statutes do not prescribe death."

sentences.zh: 上乃免文操死，顧侍臣曰：「此真諫議也！」

translations.literal: The emperor then spared Wencao from death and, turning to the attending officials, said: "This is a true remonstrating censor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then spared Wencao's life and said to those present, "This is a remonstrating censor in the true sense!"

sentences.zh: 閏月，長孫無忌等上所刪定律令式，甲戌，詔頒之四方。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, Zhangsun Wuji and others presented to the emperor the revised statutes, ordinances, and regulations; on jiaxu, an edict promulgated them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Zhangsun Wuji and others submitted the revised statutes, ordinances, and regulations; on the day jiaxu, an edict issued them throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「聞所在官司，行事猶互觀顏面，多不盡公。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers: "I hear that wherever government offices conduct affairs they still watch one another's faces and mostly do not exhaust fairness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers, "I hear that in every office men still watch one another's expressions when they act, and seldom pursue justice to the full."

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌對曰：「此豈敢言無；

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji replied: "This — who would dare say it does not exist;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji answered, "That surely exists—who would deny it?

sentences.zh: 然肆情曲法，實亦不敢。

translations.literal: yet to bend the law according to whim, in truth we also do not dare.
translations.idiomatic: But to twist the law at will—we truly do not dare either.

sentences.zh: 至於小小收取人情，恐陛下尚不能免。」

translations.literal: As for taking small favors here and there, I fear Your Majesty still cannot avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: As for petty courtesies and small favors, I fear even Your Majesty cannot wholly escape them."

sentences.zh: 無忌以元舅輔政，凡有所言，上無不嘉納。

translations.literal: Wuji, as maternal uncle assisting in government, whatever he said the emperor without exception praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's maternal uncle and chief minister, Wuji spoke with such trust that the emperor welcomed every word he offered.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛酉，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, the emperor offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔：「自今京官及外州有獻鷹隼及犬馬者，罪之。」

translations.literal: On guiyou, an edict: "From now on, capital officials and outer prefectures who present hawks, falcons, or horses will be punished."
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, an edict declared: "Henceforth any capital official or provincial officer who offers hawks, falcons, or horses will be liable to punishment."
translations.footnote: The edict's quoted passage ends here

sentences.zh: 戊寅，特浪羌酋董悉奉求、辟惠羌酋卜簷莫各帥種落萬餘戶詣茂州內附。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Telang Qiang chieftain Dong Xifengqiu and Pihui Qiang chieftain Bu Zhanmo each led more than ten thousand households of their tribes to Maozhou to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin, Telang Qiang chieftain Dong Xifengqiu and Pihui Qiang chieftain Bu Zhanmo each led tribal households numbering more than ten thousand to Maozhou to submit.

sentences.zh: 竇州、義州蠻酋李寶誠等反，桂州都督劉伯英討平之。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftains Li Baocheng and others of Dou and Yi prefectures rebelled; Gui prefecture area commander Liu Boying suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian chieftains including Li Baocheng of Dou and Yi prefectures rebelled; Gui prefecture area commander Liu Boying defeated and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 郎州道總管趙孝祖討白水蠻，蠻酋禿磨蒲及儉彌於帥眾據險拒戰，孝祖皆擊斬之。

translations.literal: Langzhou circuit overall commander Zhao Xiaozu attacked the Baishui barbarians; barbarian chieftains Tumo Pu and Jian Miyu led their followers to hold difficult terrain and resist battle; Xiaozu struck and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou circuit overall commander Zhao Xiaozu campaigned against the Baishui barbarians; chieftains Tumo Pu and Jian Miyu held the passes and fought; Xiaozu attacked and beheaded them both.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，蠻饑凍，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: Heavy snow followed; the barbarians suffered hunger and cold and died almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow then fell; the barbarians starved and froze until nearly all perished.

sentences.zh: 孝祖奏言：「貞觀中討昆州烏蠻，始開青蛉、弄棟為州縣。

translations.literal: Xiaozu memorialized: "In Zhenguan, when Kunzhou's Wuman were attacked, Qingling and Nongdong were first opened as prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu reported: "During the Zhenguan era, in the campaign against the Wuman of Kunzhou, Qingling and Nongdong were first established as prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 弄棟之西有小勃弄、大勃弄二川，恆扇誘弄棟，欲使之反。

translations.literal: West of Nongdong are the two valleys of Lesser Bonong and Greater Bonong, which constantly incite Nongdong and wish to make it rebel.
translations.idiomatic: West of Nongdong lie the Lesser and Greater Bonong valleys, which constantly stir up Nongdong and seek to turn it against us.

sentences.zh: 其勃弄以西與黃瓜、葉榆、西洱河相接，人眾殷實，多於蜀川，無大酋長，好結仇怨，今因破白水之兵，請隨便四討，撫而安之。」

translations.literal: West of Bonong it connects with Huanggua, Yeyu, and the Western Er River; the population is prosperous, greater than in Shu, with no great chieftain but a love of feuds; now, taking advantage of the army that broke the Baishui tribes, I request permission to campaign on all four sides as opportunity allows, to pacify and reassure them."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Bonong the land joins Huanggua, Yeyu, and the Western Er River; the people are numerous and wealthier than in Shu, without great chiefs but prone to vendettas. Now, with the force that defeated the Baishui tribes, I ask leave to advance on every side as occasion permits and win them by reassurance."

sentences.zh: 敕許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬子，處月朱邪孤注殺招慰使單道惠，與突厥賀魯相結。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, renzi, the Chuyue Zhuye Guzhu killed the comforting envoy Shan Daohui and allied with the Türk Helu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day renzi, the Chuyue leader Zhuye Guzhu killed the comforting envoy Shan Daohui and joined the Türk Helu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，百濟遣使入貢，上戒之，使「勿與新羅、高麗相攻，不然，吾將發兵討汝矣。」

translations.literal: That year, Baekje sent envoys to offer tribute; the emperor admonished them, saying: "Do not attack Silla and Goguryeo with one another; otherwise I shall send troops to punish you."
translations.idiomatic: That year Baekje sent tribute envoys; the emperor warned them, "Do not make war on Silla and Goguryeo together, or I shall raise an army to chastise you."
translations.footnote: The emperor's warning to Baekje ends here

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己未朔，吐谷渾、新羅、高麗、百濟並遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiwei the new moon, Tuyuhun, Silla, Goguryeo, and Baekje all sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day jiwei, Tuyuhun, Silla, Goguryeo, and Baekje each sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，梁建方、契苾何力等大破處月朱邪孤注於牢山。

translations.literal: On guihai, Liang Jianfang, Qibi Heli, and others inflicted a great defeat on the Chuyue Zhuye Guzhu at Laoshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, Liang Jianfang, Qibi Heli, and their forces routed the Chuyue leader Zhuye Guzhu at Laoshan.

sentences.zh: 孤注夜遁，建方使副總管高德逸輕騎追之，行五百餘里，生擒孤注，斬首九千級。

translations.literal: Guzhu fled by night; Jianfang sent Deputy Commander-in-Chief Gao Deyi with light cavalry in pursuit. After more than five hundred li they captured Guzhu alive and took nine thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhu fled under cover of night; Jianfang sent his deputy Gao Deyi after him with light cavalry. They rode more than five hundred li, took Guzhu alive, and counted nine thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 軍還，御史劾奏梁建方兵力足以追討，而逗留不進；

translations.literal: When the army returned, the censorate impeached Liang Jianfang, saying his force was sufficient for pursuit and punishment yet he lingered without advancing;
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the censors impeached Liang Jianfang for having strength enough to pursue the enemy yet dallying on the march;

sentences.zh: 高德逸敕令市馬，自取駿者。

translations.literal: Gao Deyi, by imperial order, bought horses and took the finest for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Deyi had been ordered to buy horses on campaign and kept the best mounts for himself.

sentences.zh: 上以建方等有功，釋不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jianfang and the others had merit, released them without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, weighing their victories, declined to press the matter.

sentences.zh: 大理卿李道裕奏言：「德逸所取之馬，筋力異常，請實中廄。」

translations.literal: Grand Court Judge Li Daoyu memorialized: "The horse Deyi took has sinew and strength beyond the ordinary; I request that it be entered in the central stables."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Court Judge Li Daoyu reported: "The horse Gao Deyi took is of extraordinary mettle; let it be registered in the imperial stud."

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「道裕法官，進馬非其本職，妄希我意；

translations.literal: The emperor told his attendants: "Daoyu is a judge; presenting a horse is not his proper duty—he presumptuously courts my favor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told those at his side: "Daoyu is a magistrate of the law; offering up a horse is outside his charge, yet he presumptuously flatters my whim—

sentences.zh: 豈朕行事不為臣下所信邪！

translations.literal: Can it be that my conduct is not trusted by my ministers!
translations.idiomatic: as if my own conduct were not trusted by the men who serve me!

sentences.zh: 朕方自咎，故不復黜道裕耳。」

translations.literal: I am just now reproaching myself, and therefore do not again dismiss Daoyu."
translations.idiomatic: I am reproaching myself just now, and so I will not dismiss Daoyu after all."
translations.footnote: The emperor's remark to his attendants ends here

sentences.zh: 己巳，以同州刺史褚遂良為吏部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On jisi, Tong Prefecture Governor Chu Suiliang was made Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi, Chu Suiliang, governor of Tong Prefecture, was appointed Minister of Personnel and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以饗太廟；

translations.literal: On bingzi, he offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，饗先農，躬耕籍田。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he sacrificed to the God of Agriculture and personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai he sacrificed to the God of Agriculture and himself turned the first furrow in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，上御安福門樓，觀百戲。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiayin, the emperor mounted the Anfu Gate tower to watch the hundred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jiayin, the emperor took the Anfu Gate tower to watch the variety shows.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上謂侍臣曰：「昨登樓，欲以觀人情及風谷奢儉，非為聲樂。

translations.literal: On yimao, the emperor told his attendants: "Yesterday when I ascended the tower, I wished to observe the people's temper and whether custom tended to luxury or frugality—not for music and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao the emperor told those beside him: "When I went up the tower yesterday, it was to read the people's mood and whether custom ran to extravagance or thrift—not for mere music and sport.

sentences.zh: 朕聞胡人善為擊鞠之戲，嘗一觀之。

translations.literal: I have heard that the Hu excel at the game of striking the ball and once watched it.
translations.idiomatic: I had heard that the northerners excel at polo and had watched it once.

sentences.zh: 昨初升樓，即有群胡擊鞠，意謂朕篤好之也。

translations.literal: Yesterday, as soon as I first mounted the tower, a crowd of Hu were already playing ball—surely they thought I doted on it.
translations.idiomatic: The moment I stepped onto the tower yesterday, a band of Hu were already at polo; they must have thought I was devoted to the game.

sentences.zh: 帝王所為，豈宜容易。

translations.literal: What a Son of Heaven does—how can it be taken lightly?
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign's least gesture should not be made lightly.

sentences.zh: 朕已焚此鞠，冀杜胡人窺望之情，亦因以自誡。」

translations.literal: I have already burned these balls, hoping to cut off the Hu people's habit of watching and guessing, and also to admonish myself thereby."
translations.idiomatic: I have burned the balls, hoping to shut off the northerners' habit of reading my whims, and to chasten myself as well."
translations.footnote: The emperor's explanation to his attendants ends here

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，以宇文節為侍中，柳奭為中書令，以兵部侍郎三原韓瑗守黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Third month, on xinsi, Yuwen Jie was made Palace Attendant, Liu Shi Director of the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of War Han Yuan of Sanyuan was made acting Yellow Gate Vice Minister and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day xinsi, Yuwen Jie became Palace Attendant, Liu Shi Director of the Secretariat, and Han Yuan of Sanyuan, vice minister of war, acting vice minister of the Yellow Gate and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，趙孝祖大破西南蠻，斬小勃弄酋長歿盛，擒大勃弄酋長楊承顛。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Zhao Xiaozu inflicted a great defeat on the southwestern barbarians, beheading the Xiaobonong chieftain Mosheng and capturing the Dabonong chieftain Yang Chengdian.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhao Xiaozu routed the southwestern tribes, beheading the Xiaobonong chieftain Mosheng and taking the Dabonong chieftain Yang Chengdian prisoner.

sentences.zh: 自餘皆屯聚保險，大者有眾數萬，小者數千人，孝祖皆破降之，西南蠻遂定。

translations.literal: The rest all gathered in strongholds in defensible terrain; the large had masses of tens of thousands, the small several thousand. Xiaozu defeated and accepted the surrender of them all, and the southwestern barbarians were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The rest had holed up in mountain fastnesses—some tens of thousands strong, others only a few thousand—and Xiaozu broke and accepted each in turn until the southwest was pacified.

sentences.zh: 甲午，澧州刺史彭思王元則薨。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Li Prefecture Governor Prince Sisi of Peng, Yuanze, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, Yuanze, Prince Sisi of Peng and governor of Li Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，遣兵部尚書崔敦禮等將並、汾步騎萬人往茂州。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wushen, dispatched Minister of War Cui Dunli and others to lead ten thousand infantry and cavalry of Bing and Fen toward Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day wushen, the court sent Minister of War Cui Dunli and others at the head of ten thousand foot and horse from Bing and Fen toward Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 發薛延陀餘眾渡河，置祁連州以處之。

translations.literal: The remaining masses of Xueyantuo were sent across the river, and Qilian Prefecture was established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving Xueyantuo were moved across the river and settled in the newly created Qilian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，立陳王忠為皇太子，赦天下。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on dingsi, Prince Chen Zhong was established as heir apparent and the empire was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day dingsi, Prince Chen Zhong was named heir apparent and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 王皇后無子，柳奭為后謀，以忠母劉氏微賤，勸皇后立忠為太子，冀其親己；

translations.literal: Empress Wang had no son; Liu Shi schemed for the empress. Because Zhong's mother, the Liu clan, was of slight and low standing, he urged the empress to establish Zhong as heir, hoping he would draw close to her;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang had borne no son; Liu Shi plotted on her behalf. Zhong's mother came of humble stock, and Liu urged the empress to name Zhong heir, hoping the boy would cling to her patronage;

sentences.zh: 外則諷長孫無忌等使請於上。

translations.literal: outwardly he prompted Zhangsun Wuji and others to request it of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: while outwardly he nudged Zhangsun Wuji and the rest to petition the throne.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以於志寧兼太子少師，張行成兼少傅，高季輔兼少保。

translations.literal: On yichou, Yu Zhining was made concurrent Junior Tutor of the Heir, Zhang Xingcheng concurrent Junior Mentor, and Gao Jifu concurrent Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, Yu Zhining was named concurrent junior tutor to the heir, Zhang Xingcheng junior mentor, and Gao Jifu junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，上問戶部尚書高履行：「去年進戶多少？」

translations.literal: On dingchou, the emperor asked Minister of Revenue Gao Lüxing: "How many households were registered last year?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou the emperor asked Minister of Revenue Gao Lüxing, "How many households were added to the rolls last year?"

sentences.zh: 履行奏：「去年進戶總一十五萬。」

translations.literal: Lüxing reported: "Last year's newly registered households totaled one hundred fifty thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Lüxing answered, "One hundred fifty thousand households in all."

sentences.zh: 因問隋代及今日見戶，履行奏：「隋開皇中，戶八百七十萬，即今戶三百八十萬。」

translations.literal: He then asked about Sui times and present registered households; Lüxing reported: "In the Kaihuang era of Sui there were eight million seven hundred thousand households; at present there are three million eight hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked about Sui and present registered households; Lüxing said, "Under Sui's Kaihuang reign there were 8.7 million households; today there are 3.8 million."

sentences.zh: 履行，士廉之子也。

translations.literal: Lüxing was the son of Shilian.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxing was a son of the late minister Gao Shilian.

sentences.zh: 九月，守中書侍郎來濟同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Ninth month, acting Secretariat Vice Minister Lai Ji was made Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Lai Ji, acting vice minister of the Secretariat, became associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，庚寅，弘化長公主自吐谷渾來朝。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on gengyin, the Princess of Great Transformation came from Tuyuhun to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day gengyin, the Princess of Honghua came from Tuyuhun to pay homage at court.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，濮恭王泰薨於均州。

translations.literal: On guisi, Prince Gong of Pu, Tai, died at Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Li Tai, Prince Gong of Pu, died in exile at Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍房遺愛尚太宗女高陽公主，公主驕恣甚，房玄齡薨，公主教遺愛與兄遺直異財，既而反譖遺直。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fang Yi'an married Emperor Taizong's daughter Princess Gaoyang; the princess was exceedingly arrogant and willful. When Fang Xuanling died, the princess instructed Yi'an and his elder brother Yizhi to divide the property unequally, then in turn slandered Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fang Yi'an had married Emperor Taizong's daughter, Princess Gaoyang, a woman of fierce pride. After Fang Xuanling's death the princess set Yi'an against his elder brother Yizhi over the estate, then turned and accused Yizhi falsely.

sentences.zh: 遺直自言，太宗深責讓主，由是寵衰，主怏怏不悅。

translations.literal: Yizhi spoke for himself; Taizong deeply reproached the princess, and from this her favor waned. The princess was resentful and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi spoke in his own defense, Taizong rebuked the princess sharply; her favor faded, and she nursed a sullen grievance.

sentences.zh: 會御史劾盜，得浮屠辯機寶枕，雲主所賜。

translations.literal: It happened that the censorate impeached a theft and recovered the Buddhist monk Bianji's jeweled pillow, said to have been bestowed by the princess.
translations.idiomatic: A theft investigation by the censors turned up a jeweled pillow belonging to the monk Bianji, said to be the princess's gift.

sentences.zh: 主與辯機私通，餉遺億計，更以二女子侍遺愛。

translations.literal: The princess had a secret liaison with Bianji; gifts to him ran to hundreds of millions, and she further gave two women to attend Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: She had been carrying on with Bianji, lavishing gifts beyond counting, and even sent two women to wait on Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，腰斬辯機，殺奴婢十餘人；

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged, cut Bianji in two at the waist, and killed more than ten slave women;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's rage fell on Bianji, who was cut in two at the waist, and on more than a dozen of her servants besides;

sentences.zh: 主益怨望，太宗崩，無戚容。

translations.literal: the princess grew still more resentful. When Taizong died she showed no look of grief.
translations.idiomatic: yet the princess only grew more bitter. When Taizong died she wore no mourning face.

sentences.zh: 上即位，主又令遺愛與遺直更相訟，遺愛坐出為房州刺史，遺直為隰州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, the princess again had Yi'an and Yizhi sue one another. Yi'an was demoted to governor of Fang Prefecture; Yizhi became governor of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the new emperor's accession she set Yi'an and Yizhi at law again; Yi'an was sent out as governor of Fang Prefecture and Yizhi of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又，浮屠智勖等數人私侍主，主使掖庭令陳玄運伺宮省禨祥。

translations.literal: Moreover, the monks Zhi Xu and several others privately attended the princess; she had Palace Women's Director Chen Xuanyun watch the palace precincts for omens of fortune or ill.
translations.idiomatic: Monks including Zhi Xu attended her in secret, and she set Palace Women's Director Chen Xuanyun to watch the inner quarters for omens.

sentences.zh: 先是，駙馬都尉薛萬徹坐事除名，徙寧州刺史，入朝，與遺愛款暱，對遺愛有怨望語，且曰：「今雖病足，坐置京師，鼠輩猶不敢動。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Commandant of Escort Xue Wanche, punished for an offense, was struck from the rolls and transferred to governor of Ning Prefecture. On entering court he was intimate with Yi'an and spoke to him words of resentment, saying: "Though my feet are ill now, were I merely seated in the capital, not one of those rats would dare stir."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chief Commandant of Escort Xue Wanche had been struck from the rolls for an offense and made governor of Ning Prefecture. Back at court he grew close to Yi'an and let slip bitter words: "Though my feet ail me, set me in the capital and not one of those rats would dare move."

sentences.zh: 因與遺愛謀：「若國家有變，當奉司徒荊王元景為主。」

translations.literal: He then plotted with Yi'an: "If the state should change, we ought to set up Situ Prince Jing Yuanjing as ruler."
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted with Yi'an: "Should the realm fall into turmoil, we must set up Situ Prince Jing, Yuanjing, as sovereign."

sentences.zh: 元景女適遺愛弟遺則，由是與遺愛往來。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's daughter was married to Yi'an's younger brother Yize; for this reason he associated with Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's daughter had married Yi'an's younger brother Yize, which drew him into Yi'an's circle.

sentences.zh: 元景嘗自言，夢手把日月。

translations.literal: Yuanjing once said of himself that he dreamed of holding sun and moon in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing once boasted that he had dreamed of holding the sun and moon in his hands.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉柴令武，紹之子也，尚巴陵公主，除衛州刺史，托以主疾留京師求醫，因與遺愛謀議相結。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant of Escort Chai Lingwu, son of Shao, married Princess Baling, was made governor of Wei Prefecture, pleaded his wife's illness to remain in the capital seeking medicine, and thereby joined in plotting with Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant of Escort Chai Lingwu, a son of Chai Shao, had married Princess Baling and been made governor of Wei Prefecture; he pleaded his wife's illness to stay in the capital for treatment and there bound himself to Yi'an's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 高陽公主謀黜遺直，奪其封爵，使人誣告遺直無禮於己。

translations.literal: Princess Gaoyang plotted to remove Yizhi and seize his enfeoffment and rank, sending men to accuse him falsely of discourtesy toward herself.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Gaoyang schemed to strip Yizhi of title and fief, sending agents to accuse him of insulting her.

sentences.zh: 遺直亦言遺愛及主罪，云：「罪盈惡稔，恐累臣私門。」

translations.literal: Yizhi also reported the crimes of Yi'an and the princess, saying: "Their crimes overflow and wickedness is ripe; I fear they will implicate my private household."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi in turn denounced Yi'an and the princess, saying, "Their guilt is full to overflowing; I fear it will drag down our whole clan."

sentences.zh: 上令長孫無忌鞫之，更獲遺愛及主反狀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji to try the case and further obtained evidence of rebellion by Yi'an and the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Zhangsun Wuji in charge of the inquiry, and still more proof of Yi'an and the princess's treason came to light.

sentences.zh: 司空、安州都督吳王恪母，隋煬帝女也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and An Prefecture Protector-General Prince of Wu, Ke—his mother was a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ke of Wu, minister of works and protector-general of An Prefecture, was born of a daughter of Emperor Yang of Sui.

sentences.zh: 恪有文武才，太宗常以為類己，欲立為太子，無忌固爭而止，由是與無忌相惡。

translations.literal: Ke had civil and military talent; Taizong often thought him like himself and wished to establish him as heir, but Wuji firmly contested it and stopped this—whereupon Ke and Wuji came to hate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ke possessed both civil and martial gifts; Taizong often found him like himself and once meant to name him heir, until Wuji's stubborn opposition blocked it—and from that day Ke and Wuji were enemies.

sentences.zh: 恪名望素高，為物情所向，無忌深忌之，欲因事誅恪以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Ke's fame and standing had long been high; popular sentiment turned toward him. Wuji deeply feared him and wished to use the affair to execute Ke and cut off the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's renown had always stood high and men's hearts turned to him; Wuji hated him bitterly and meant to use the case to kill him and break the public's hopes.

sentences.zh: 遺愛知之，因言與恪同謀，冀如紇干承基得免死。

translations.literal: Yi'an knew this and therefore said he had plotted together with Ke, hoping that like Gan Chengji he might escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Yi'an saw his chance and claimed Ke as co-conspirator, hoping that as Gan Chengji had once done he might trade accusation for his life.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，甲申，詔遺愛、萬徹、令武皆斬，元景，恪、高陽、巴陵公主並賜自盡。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on jiashen, an edict ordered Yi'an, Wanche, and Lingwu all beheaded; Yuanjing, Ke, Gaoyang, and the Princess of Baling were all granted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on the day jiashen, an edict beheaded Yi'an, Wanche, and Lingwu; Yuanjing, Ke, Princess Gaoyang, and Princess Baling were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 上潤謂侍臣曰：「荊王，朕之叔父，吳王，朕兄，欲丐其死，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor, with moistened voice, told his attendants: "Prince Jing is my father's younger brother; Prince Wu is my elder brother. I wish to beg their lives—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: With tears in his voice the emperor asked his attendants, "Prince Jing is my uncle, Prince Wu my elder brother—may I beg their lives?"

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書崔敦禮以為不可，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Cui Dunli held it impossible, and so they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Cui Dunli said it could not be done, and they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 萬徹臨刑大言曰：「薛萬徹大健兒，留為國家效死力，豈不佳，乃坐房遺愛殺之乎！」

translations.literal: At execution Wanche cried out loudly: "Xue Wanche is a great stalwart—leave him to spend his strength dying for the state, would that not be better? Yet he is killed because he sat with Fang Yi'an!"
translations.idiomatic: At the block Wanche shouted, "Xue Wanche is a fighting man—leave him to die for the state, would that not serve better than killing him for sitting with Fang Yi'an!"

sentences.zh: 吳王恪且死，罵曰：「長孫無忌竊弄威權，構害良善，宗社有靈，當族滅不久！」

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Ke, about to die, cursed: "Zhangsun Wuji usurps and wields authority, frames and harms the good—if the altars of state have spirit, his clan will be extinguished before long!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ke of Wu, facing death, cursed: "Zhangsun Wuji steals power and ruins the innocent—if the spirits of the realm live, his house will be wiped out ere long!"
translations.footnote: Prince Ke's dying curse ends here

sentences.zh: 乙酉，侍中兼太子詹事宇文節，特進、太常卿江夏王道宗、左驍衛大將軍駙馬都尉執失思力並坐與房遺愛交通，流嶺表。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Palace Attendant and concurrent Heir Apparent Steward Yuwen Jie, Special Advancement and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Prince Daizong of Jiangxia, and Left Swift Tiger Guards General Chief Commandant of Escort Zhisi Heli were all punished for association with Fang Yi'an and exiled beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Yuwen Jie, palace attendant and steward to the heir; Prince Daizong of Jiangxia; and Zhisi Heli, left swift tiger guards general and chief commandant of escort—all were banished beyond the mountains for ties to Fang Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 節與遺愛親善，及遺愛下獄，節頗左右之。

translations.literal: Jie had been on friendly terms with Yi'an; when Yi'an was cast into prison, Jie had somewhat aided him on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had been close to Yi'an and, once Yi'an was imprisoned, had tried to shield him.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗素與長孫無忌、褚遂良不協，故皆得罪。

translations.literal: Prince Daizong of Jiangxia had long been at odds with Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang; for this reason they all fell into guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daizong of Jiangxia had long been at odds with Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang, and so he too was swept into the net.

sentences.zh: 戊子，廢恪母弟蜀王愔為庶人，置巴州；

translations.literal: On wuzi, Ke's younger brother by the same mother, Prince Min of Shu, Yin, was demoted to commoner status and settled in Ba Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, Ke's uterine brother, Prince Yin of Shu, was reduced to commoner rank and confined in Ba Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 房遺直貶春州銅陵尉，萬徹弟萬備流交州；

translations.literal: Fang Yizhi was demoted to district magistrate of Tongling in Chun Prefecture; Wanche's younger brother Wanbei was exiled to Jiao Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yizhi was demoted to magistrate of Tongling in Chun Prefecture; Wanche's brother Wanbei was sent to Jiao Prefecture in exile;

sentences.zh: 罷房玄齡配饗。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling's paired sacrifice in the ancestral temple was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: and Fang Xuanling was stripped of his place at the paired sacrifices in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司李勣為司空。

translations.literal: Honored Attendant of the First Order Li Ji was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, honored attendant of the first order, was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，林邑王范頭利卒，子真龍立，大臣伽獨弒之，盡滅范氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, the king of Linyi, Fantouli, died; his son Zhenlong was established, but the great minister Jiadue assassinated him and extinguished the Fan clan entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Fantouli of Linyi had died and his son Zhenlong succeeded; the great minister Jiadue murdered him and wiped out the Fan line.

sentences.zh: 伽獨自立，國人弗從，乃立頭利之婿婆羅門為王。

translations.literal: Jiadue declared himself ruler, but the people would not follow; they therefore established Fantouli's son-in-law Brahmana as king.
translations.idiomatic: Jiadue seized the throne, but the people refused him and set up Fantouli's son-in-law Brahmana instead.

sentences.zh: 國人鹹思范氏，復罷婆羅門，立頭利之女為王。

translations.literal: The people all yearned for the Fan clan; they again deposed Brahmana and established Fantouli's daughter as king.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still longed for the Fan house, deposed Brahmana again, and enthroned Fantouli's daughter.

sentences.zh: 女不能治國，有諸葛地者，頭利之姑子也，父為頭利所殺，南奔真臘，大臣可倫翁定遣使迎而立之，妻以女王，眾然後定。

translations.literal: The woman could not govern the state. There was one Zhugedi, Fantouli's nephew by marriage; his father had been killed by Fantouli, and he had fled south to Zhenla. The great minister Kelun Wengding sent envoys to welcome and establish him, marrying him to the queen; only then did the multitude settle.
translations.idiomatic: She could not rule; a man named Zhugedi, Fantouli's nephew by marriage whose father Fantouli had killed, had fled south to Zhenla. The minister Kelun Wengding fetched him back, married him to the queen, and only then did the kingdom find peace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊子，遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on wuzi, envoys were sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wuzi, Linyi sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，壬戌，右僕射北平定公張行成薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, on renxu, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Duke Ding of Beiping, Zhang Xingcheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day renxu, Zhang Xingcheng, right vice director and Duke Ding of Beiping, died.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以褚遂良為右僕射，同中書門下三品如故，仍知選事。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Chu Suiliang was made Right Vice Director, remaining Associate Grand Councilor as before, and still in charge of selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, Chu Suiliang became right vice director, kept his seat as associate grand councilor, and continued to oversee appointments.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚子，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on gengzi, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengzi, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: On yisi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 初，睦州女子陳碩貞以妖言惑眾，與妹夫章叔胤舉兵反，自稱文佳皇帝，以叔胤為僕射。

translations.literal: Earlier, a woman of Muzhou, Chen Shuozhen, deluded the masses with demonic speech. With her brother-in-law Zhang Shuyin she raised troops in rebellion, styled herself Emperor Wenjia, and made Shuyin Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen Shuozhen of Muzhou had swayed the people with sorcerous talk; with her brother-in-law Zhang Shuyin she rose in arms, crowned herself Emperor Wenjia, and named Shuyin her chief minister.

sentences.zh: 甲子夜，叔胤帥眾攻桐廬，陷之。

translations.literal: On the night of jiazi, Shuyin led the masses to attack Tonglu and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the day jiazi, Shuyin led his followers against Tonglu and took the city.

sentences.zh: 碩真撞鐘焚香，引兵二千攻陷睦州及於潛，進攻歙州，不克。

translations.literal: Shuozhen struck the bell and burned incense, led two thousand troops to capture Muzhou and Yuqian, advanced to attack She Prefecture, and did not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhen rang bells and burned incense, marched two thousand men to seize Muzhou and Yuqian, then pushed against She Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 敕揚州刺史房仁裕發兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Prefecture Governor Fang Renyu to mobilize troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Fang Renyu, governor of Yang Prefecture, to take the field against them.

sentences.zh: 碩真遣其黨童文寶將四千人寇婺州，刺史崔義玄發兵拒之。

translations.literal: Shuozhen sent her partisan Tong Wenbao to lead four thousand men to raid Wu Prefecture; Governor Cui Yixuan mobilized troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhen sent her lieutenant Tong Wenbao with four thousand men against Wu Prefecture; Governor Cui Yixuan marched out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 民間訛言碩真有神，犯其兵者必滅族，士眾兇懼。

translations.literal: Among the people a false rumor spread that Shuozhen had divine power and that whoever opposed her troops would surely have his clan extinguished; soldiers and masses were violently afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors ran that Shuozhen wielded divine power and that any who faced her army would see their clans wiped out; the troops were seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 司功參軍崔玄籍曰：「起兵仗順，猶且無成，況憑妖妄，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: Records Section Aide Cui Xuanji said: "Those who raise troops relying on righteousness still may not succeed—how much less those who depend on demonic delusion? How could they last long!"
translations.idiomatic: Records aide Cui Xuanji said, "Men who take up arms in a just cause still often fail—how long can sorcery and delusion hold!"

sentences.zh: 義玄以玄籍為前鋒，自將州兵繼之，至下淮戍，遇賊，與戰。

translations.literal: Yixuan made Xuanji vanguard, himself leading prefectural troops after him. They reached Xiahuai garrison, encountered the rebels, and fought.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan put Xuanji in the van and followed with the prefectural force; at Xiahuai garrison they met the rebels and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 左右以楯蔽義玄，義玄曰：「刺史避箭，人誰致死！」

translations.literal: Those at his sides used shields to screen Yixuan; Yixuan said: "If the governor dodges arrows, who will die for him!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants raised shields before him; Yixuan cried, "If the governor ducks arrows, who will die for him!

sentences.zh: 命撤之。

translations.literal: He ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the shields taken away.

sentences.zh: 於是士卒齊奮，賊眾大潰，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers all strove together; the rebel masses collapsed in great rout, and several thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: At that the men fought as one; the rebels broke and fled, leaving several thousand heads on the field.

sentences.zh: 聽其餘眾歸首；

translations.literal: The rest of the masses were allowed to return and surrender;
translations.idiomatic: The survivors were allowed to surrender;

sentences.zh: 進至睦州境，降者萬計。

translations.literal: advancing to the border of Muzhou, those who submitted numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: and by the time he reached Muzhou's border, tens of thousands had come over.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，房仁裕軍合，獲碩真、叔胤，斬之，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on gengxu, Fang Renyu's armies united, captured Shuozhen and Shuyin, beheaded them, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day gengxu, Fang Renyu's columns joined, took Shuozhen and Shuyin, and beheaded them; the remnant rebels were swept clean.

sentences.zh: 義玄以功拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Yixuan, for his merit, was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Cui Yixuan was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以兵部尚書崔敦禮為侍中。

translations.literal: On guichou, Minister of War Cui Dunli was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, Cui Dunli, minister of war, was appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，侍中蓨憲公高季輔薨。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on gengzi, Palace Attendant Duke Xian of Tiao, Gao Jifu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, Gao Jifu, palace attendant and Duke Xian of Tiao, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，西突厥乙毘咄陸可汗卒，其子頡苾達度設號真珠葉護，始與沙缽羅可汗有隙，與五弩失畢共擊沙缽羅，破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: That year, the Western Türk qaghan Yipiduolu died; his son Tegin Yipishdabodu styled himself True Pearl yabghu. At first he had a rift with the qaghan Shaboluo; together with the Five Nushibi he attacked Shaboluo, defeated him, and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Western Türk qaghan Yipiduolu died; his son Yipishdabodu took the title True Pearl yabghu. He had fallen out with the qaghan Shaboluo and, joining the Five Nushibi, routed Shaboluo and counted more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，羌酋凍就內附，以其地置劍州。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on renxu, the Qiang chieftain Dong Jiu submitted to the interior; his territory was established as Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the day renxu, the Qiang chieftain Dong Jiu came in to allegiance, and his lands were organized as Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午，上行幸萬年宮。

translations.literal: Third month, on wuwu, the emperor traveled in person to Wannian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day wuwu, the emperor went in person to Wannian Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚申，加贈武德功臣屈突通等十三人官。

translations.literal: On gengshen, posthumously added ranks for the thirteen Merit Ministers of the Wude era including Qu Tu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen, the court posthumously promoted the ranks of thirteen Wude-era merit ministers, among them Qu Tu Tong.

sentences.zh: 初，王皇后無子，蕭淑妃有寵，王后疾子。

translations.literal: Initially, Empress Wang had no sons; Consort Xiao the Pure and Fair had favor; the empress resented her.
translations.idiomatic: At first Empress Wang had borne no sons, while Consort Xiao the Pure and Fair held the emperor's favor, and the empress came to resent her.

sentences.zh: 上之為太子也，入侍太宗，見才人武氏而悅之。

translations.literal: When he was crown prince, attending Emperor Taizong, he saw the Lady of Talents Wu and was pleased with her.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, attending at Emperor Taizong's side, he saw the Lady of Talents of the Wu clan and took a liking to her.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，武氏隨眾感業寺為尼。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Wu followed the multitude to Gan'ye Temple and became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death, Lady Wu went with the other consorts to Gan'ye Temple and took the tonsure.

sentences.zh: 忌日，上詣寺行香，見之，武氏泣，上亦泣。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of his death, the emperor went to the temple to burn incense, saw her; Wu wept, the emperor also wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Taizong's death the emperor went to the temple to offer incense, saw her again, and they wept together.

sentences.zh: 王后聞之，陰令武氏長髮，勸上內之後宮，欲以間淑妃之寵。

translations.literal: Empress Wang heard of it, secretly had Wu grow her hair long, urged the emperor to bring her into the inner palace, wishing to use her to come between Consort Xiao's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang heard of this, secretly had Wu let her hair grow again, and urged the emperor to take her back into the inner palace, hoping to use her to break Consort Xiao's hold on him.

sentences.zh: 武氏巧慧，多權數，初入宮，卑辭屈體以事后。

translations.literal: Wu was clever and artful, with many stratagems; newly entering the palace, she used humble words and bowed her body to serve the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resourceful, full of schemes, she entered the palace and humbled herself in word and bearing to wait on the empress.

sentences.zh: 后愛之，數稱其美於上。

translations.literal: The empress loved her, repeatedly praised her beauty to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress grew fond of her and often praised her to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 未幾大幸，拜為昭儀，后及淑妃寵皆衰，更相與共譖之，上皆不納。

translations.literal: Before long she received great favor, was appointed Lady of Bright Deportment; the empress and the Pure and Fair Consort's favor both declined; they moreover joined each other in slandering her, but the emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she won his deepest favor and was made Lady of Bright Deportment; favor for the empress and Consort Xiao waned, and the two began slandering her together, but the emperor would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 昭儀欲追贈其父而無名，故托以褒賞功臣，遍贈屈突通等，而武士擭預焉。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment wished to posthumously ennoble her father but had no title; therefore she used as pretext rewarding merit ministers, extending ennoblements to Qu Tu Tong and others, and Wu Shiyao was included among them.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to have her father honored posthumously but lacked a plausible claim, so she arranged a general reward of merit ministers—Qu Tu Tong and the rest—and slipped her father Wu Shiyao into the list.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，上幸鳳泉湯；

translations.literal: On yichou, the emperor visited Fengquan Hot Springs;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou the emperor visited the Fengquan hot springs;

sentences.zh: 己巳，還萬年宮。

translations.literal: On jisi, returned to Wannian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jisi he returned to Wannian Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，大食發兵擊波斯，殺波斯王伊嗣侯，伊嗣侯之子卑路斯奔吐火羅。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Arabs sent troops to attack Persia, killed the Persian king Yazdegerd; Yazdegerd's son Peroz fled to Tokhara.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Arab forces marched on Persia, killed King Yazdegerd, and his son Peroz fled to Tokhara.

sentences.zh: 大食兵去，吐火羅發兵立卑路斯為波斯王而還。

translations.literal: When the Arab troops departed, Tokhara sent troops to install Peroz as Persian king and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Arab army withdrew, Tokhara raised an army, installed Peroz as king of Persia, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙子，以處月部置金滿州。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on bingzi, the Chuyue tribe was established as Jinman Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day bingzi, the Chuyue people were organized as Jinman Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，夜，大雨，山水漲溢，沖玄武門，宿衛士皆散走。

translations.literal: On dingchou, at night, heavy rain; mountains and streams swelled and overflowed, striking the Xuanwu Gate; night guards all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of dingchou a great rain fell; mountain torrents burst forth, smashed through the Xuanwu Gate, and the night guards fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 右領軍郎將薛仁貴曰：「安有宿衛之士，天子有急而敢畏死乎！」

translations.literal: Right Adjutant of the Right Wing Army Xue Rengui said: "How can there be night guards who, when the Son of Heaven is in peril, dare fear death!"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengui, adjutant of the Right Wing Army, cried, "What night guard flees when the Son of Heaven is in danger and dares cling to his own life!"

sentences.zh: 乃登門桄大呼以警宮內。

translations.literal: He then climbed the gate lintel and shouted loudly to alert the palace interior.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the gate lintel and shouted until the whole inner palace was roused.

sentences.zh: 上遽出乘高，俄而水入寢殿，水漂溺衛士及麟游居人，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor hurried out to higher ground; soon water entered the sleeping hall; water drowned guards and Linyou residents—more than three thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to high ground; moments later floodwater poured into the sleeping hall, drowning guards and townsfolk of Linyou—more than three thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，新羅女王金真德卒，詔立其弟春秋為新羅王。

translations.literal: On renchen, Queen of Silla Kim Jeongdeok died; an edict installed her brother Chungch'ul as king of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen Queen Kim Jeongdeok of Silla died; the court decreed that her brother Chungch'ul should succeed as king.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午，恆州大水，呼沱溢，漂溺五千三百家。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on bingwu, Heng Prefecture great flood; Hutuo overflowed, drowning five thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingwu, Heng Prefecture was struck by flood; the Hutuo burst its banks and swept away fifty-three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 中書令柳奭以王皇后寵衰，內不自安，請解政事；

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Secretariat Liu Shi, because Empress Wang's favor had declined, inwardly ill at ease, requested to be relieved of government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, chancellor of the Secretariat, uneasy as Empress Wang's influence waned, asked to be relieved of office;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，罷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On guihai, was dismissed and made Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he was removed and made minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，丁酉，車駕至京師。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, on dingyou, the imperial carriage reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on dingyou, the imperial procession reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，上謂五品以上曰：「頃在先帝左右，見五品以上論事，或仗下面陳，或退上封事，終日不絕；

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor addressed those of fifth rank and above, saying: "Recently at the late emperor's side, I saw those of fifth rank and above discussing affairs—some would state them below staff in person, some would submit sealed memorials after retiring—never ceasing all day;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he addressed officials of the fifth rank and above: "When I stood at the late emperor's side, men of your rank debated policy all day—some speaking below the hall, some submitting sealed memorials after court—without pause;

sentences.zh: 豈今日獨無事邪，何公等皆不言也？」

translations.literal: can it be that today alone there are no affairs? Why do you all not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: has the realm today no business at all, that none of you will speak?"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，雇雍州四萬一千人築長安外郭，三旬而畢。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, hired forty-one thousand men of Yong Prefecture to build Chang'an's outer wall; finished in thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, forty-one thousand laborers from Yong Prefecture were hired to raise Chang'an's outer wall; the work was finished in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，雍州參軍薛景宣上封事，言：「漢惠帝城長安，尋晏駕；

translations.literal: On guichou, Yong Prefecture aide Xue Jingxuan submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Emperor Huidi of Han walled Chang'an, and soon after died in his prime;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Xue Jingxuan, an aide of Yong Prefecture, submitted a sealed memorial: "When Emperor Huidi of Han walled Chang'an, he soon died in his prime;

sentences.zh: 今復城之，必有大咎。」

translations.literal: now if we wall it again, there will surely be great misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: if we wall it again now, great calamity is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 於志寧等以景宣言涉不順，請誅之。

translations.literal: Yu Zhining and others, because Jingxuan's words touched on rebellion, requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining and others said Jingxuan's words smacked of sedition and asked that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「景宣雖狂妄，若因上封事得罪，恐絕言路。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though Jingxuan is wild and reckless, if he were punished for submitting a sealed memorial, I fear the path of speech would be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jingxuan may be rash, but to punish a man for a sealed memorial would choke off honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂赦之。

translations.literal: He therefore pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣其將安固將高麗、靺鞨兵擊契丹；

translations.literal: Goryeo sent its general An Gu leading Goryeo and Mohe troops to attack the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent the general An Gu at the head of Goryeo and Mohe forces against the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 松漠都督李窟哥御之，大敗高麗於新城。

translations.literal: Protectorate General of Songmo Li Kugo resisted them and greatly defeated Goryeo at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kugo, protector-general of Songmo, met them and routed the Goryeo army at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲大稔，洛州粟米斗兩錢半，粳米斗十一錢。

translations.literal: That year there was a great harvest; Luoyang millet was two and a half cash per dou, polished rice eleven cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a bumper harvest; in Luoyang millet sold for two and a half cash a dou and polished rice for eleven.

sentences.zh: 王皇后、蕭淑妃與武昭儀更相譖訴，上不信后、淑妃之語，獨信昭儀。

translations.literal: Empress Wang, Consort Xiao the Pure and Fair, and the Lady of Bright Deportment Wu successively slandered each other; the emperor did not believe the empress and the Pure and Fair Consort's words, believing only the Lady of Bright Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang, Consort Xiao, and Lady Wu of Bright Deportment traded accusations; the emperor dismissed the empress and Consort Xiao and believed only Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 后不能曲事上左右，母魏國夫人柳氏及舅中書令柳奭入見六宮，又不為禮。

translations.literal: The empress could not defer to those at the emperor's side; her mother Lady of Wei State Liu and her uncle Chancellor Liu Shi entered to see the six palaces, and again did not observe propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The empress would not court those about the emperor; her mother, Lady Liu of Wei State, and her uncle Liu Shi, chancellor of the Secretariat, visited the six palaces without proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 武昭儀伺后所不敬者，必傾心與相結，所得賞賜分與之。

translations.literal: Lady Wu of Bright Deportment watched for those the empress did not respect, invariably devoted her heart to associating with them, and divided gifts received among them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu noted everyone the empress slighted, won them with her full attention, and shared her rewards with them.

sentences.zh: 由是后及淑妃動靜，昭儀必知之，皆以聞於上。

translations.literal: Thus the empress and the Pure and Fair Consort's every move, the Lady of Bright Deportment necessarily knew, and all reported them to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hence every move of the empress and Consort Xiao reached Lady Wu, and she reported it all to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 后寵雖衰，然上未有意廢也。

translations.literal: Though the empress's favor had declined, yet the emperor had no intent to depose her.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empress had lost favor, the emperor still had no thought of deposing her.

sentences.zh: 會昭儀生女，后憐而弄之，后出，昭儀潛扼殺之，覆之以被。

translations.literal: When the Lady of Bright Deportment bore a daughter, the empress pitied her and played with her; the empress left, and the Lady of Bright Deportment secretly strangled the child and covered it with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wu bore a daughter, the empress took pity on the infant and played with her; after the empress left, Lady Wu secretly smothered the child and drew a quilt over the body.

sentences.zh: 上至，昭儀陽歡笑，發被觀之，女已死矣，即驚啼。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, the Lady of Bright Deportment pretended mirth, lifted the quilt to look—the girl was already dead, and at once wailed in shock.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came in, Lady Wu feigned cheer, lifted the quilt—and at the sight of the dead child burst into shocked wailing.

sentences.zh: 問左右，左右皆曰：「皇后適來此。」

translations.literal: He asked those about; all said: "The empress had just come here."
translations.idiomatic: He questioned those about her; all said, "The empress had just been here."

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「后殺吾女！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and said: "The empress killed my daughter!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage: "The empress killed my child!"

sentences.zh: 昭儀因泣訴其罪。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment then wept and stated her accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu wept and pressed the charge.

sentences.zh: 后無以自明，上由是有廢立之志。

translations.literal: The empress could not clear herself; the emperor from this had the will to depose and install.
translations.idiomatic: The empress could not clear herself, and from that day the emperor resolved to depose her and raise another.

sentences.zh: 又畏大臣不從，乃與昭儀幸太尉長孫無忌第，酣飲極歡，席上拜無忌寵姬子三人皆為朝散大夫，仍載金寶繒錦十車以賜無忌。

translations.literal: Also fearing that great ministers would not follow, he therefore with the Lady of Bright Deportment visited Grand Mentor Chang Sun Wuji's residence, drank to the utmost in great joy, at table enfeoffed Wuji's three sons by his favorite concubine all as Court Gentlemen for Scattered Service, and moreover loaded ten carts of gold, jewels, silks, and brocades to bestow on Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the chief ministers would refuse, he visited Grand Mentor Chang Sun Wuji with Lady Wu, drank deep in feigned intimacy, enfeoffed Wuji's three sons by a favorite concubine as court gentlemen for scattered service at table, and sent ten cartloads of gold, gems, silk, and brocade as gifts.

sentences.zh: 上因從容言皇后無子以諷無忌，無忌對以他語，竟不順旨，上及昭儀皆不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore calmly spoke of the empress having no sons to hint at Wuji; Wuji replied with other topics, in the end not following his intent; the emperor and the Lady of Bright Deportment were both displeased and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor casually remarked that the empress had no sons, hoping Wuji would take the hint; Wuji answered on other matters and never yielded; emperor and Lady Wu left displeased.

sentences.zh: 昭儀又令母楊氏詣無忌第，屢有祈請，無忌終不許。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment also had her mother the Lady Yang visit Wuji's residence, repeatedly pleading; Wuji in the end did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu sent her mother Lady Yang to Wuji's house again and again to plead; Wuji still refused.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書許敬宗亦數勸無忌，無忌厲色折之。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong also repeatedly urged Wuji; Wuji sternly rebuffed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, minister of rites, also pressed Wuji several times; Wuji rebuffed him with a harsh face.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申朔，上謁昭陵；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on renshen the first day of the month, the emperor visited Zhaoling;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the day renshen, the emperor visited Zhaoling;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jiaxu he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 己丑，巂州道行軍總管曹繼叔破胡叢、顯養、車魯等蠻於斜山，拔十餘城。

translations.literal: On jichou, Commander of the Campaign Army of the Qiongzhou Circuit Cao Jishu broke the Hu Cong, Xianyang, Chelu, and other tribes of barbarians at Xieshan and took more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Cao Jishu, commander of the Qiongzhou campaign army, defeated the Hu Cong, Xianyang, Chelu, and other southern tribes at Xieshan and seized more than ten cities.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，立皇子弘為代王，賢為潞王。

translations.literal: On gengyin, installed the princes Hong as Prince of Dai and Xian as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the princes Hong and Xian were invested as Prince of Dai and Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 高麗與百濟、靺鞨連兵，侵新羅北境，取三十三城；

translations.literal: Goryeo together with Baekje and Mohe joined armies, invaded Silla's northern border, and took thirty-three cities;
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo allied with Baekje and the Mohe, invaded Silla's northern marches, and seized thirty-three cities;

sentences.zh: 新羅王春秋遣使求援。

translations.literal: King of Silla Chungch'ul sent an envoy requesting aid.
translations.idiomatic: King Chungch'ul of Silla sent envoys begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，遣營州都督程名振、左衛中郎將蘇定方發兵擊高麗。

translations.literal: Second month, on yichou, sent Protectorate General of Ying Prefecture Cheng Mingzhen and Colonel of the Left Guard Center Su Dingfang to launch troops and attack Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, Cheng Mingzhen, protector-general of Ying Prefecture, and Su Dingfang, colonel of the Left Guard Center, were sent to strike Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬午，名振等渡遼水，高麗見其兵少，開門渡貴端水逆戰。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, on renwu, Mingzhen and others crossed the Liao River; Goryeo, seeing their few troops, opened the gates and crossed the Guiduan River to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on renwu, Mingzhen crossed the Liao; seeing how few his men were, Goryeo sallied across the Guiduan to give battle.

sentences.zh: 名振等奮擊，大破之，殺獲千餘人，焚其外郭及村落而還。

translations.literal: Mingzhen and others strove in attack, greatly defeated them, killed and captured more than a thousand men, burned their outer wall and villages, and returned.
