translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen attacked fiercely, routed them, killed or captured more than a thousand, burned the outer walls and villages, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以右屯衛大將軍程知節為蔥山道行軍大總管，以討西突厥沙缽羅可汗。

translations.literal: On guimao, appointed General of the Right Rear Guard Cheng Zhijie as Grand Commander of the Onion Mountain Campaign Army to attack the Western Türk qaghan Shaboluo.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Cheng Zhijie, general of the Right Rear Guard, was made grand commander of the Onion Mountain campaign to attack the Western Türk qaghan Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以韓瑗為侍中，來濟為中書令。

translations.literal: On renchen, appointed Han Yuan as Palace Attendant and Lai Ji as Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Han Yuan was made palace attendant and Lai Ji chancellor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六月，武昭儀誣王后與其母魏國夫人柳氏為厭勝，敕禁后母柳氏不得入宮。

translations.literal: Sixth month, the Lady of Bright Deportment Wu falsely accused Empress Wang and her mother Lady of Wei State Liu of witchcraft; an edict forbade the empress's mother Lady Liu from entering the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Lady Wu accused Empress Wang and her mother Lady Liu of Wei State of sorcery; an edict barred the empress's mother from the palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，貶吏部尚書柳奭為遂州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on wuyin, demoted Minister of Civil Appointments Liu Shi to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Liu Shi, minister of civil appointments, was demoted to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 奭行至扶風，岐州長史於承素希旨奏奭漏洩禁中語，復貶榮州刺史。

translations.literal: When Liu Shi reached Fufeng, the prefectural administrator Yu Chengsu, to please superiors, memorialized that Liu Shi leaked forbidden-palace words; he was again demoted to prefect of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At Fufeng, Yu Chengsu, chief secretary of Qizhou, eager to please, memorialized that Liu Shi had leaked palace secrets; he was demoted again to prefect of Rong.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋制，後宮有貴妃、淑妃、德妃、賢妃皆視一品。

translations.literal: Tang followed Sui institutions: the inner palace had Noble Consort, Pure and Fair Consort, Virtuous Consort, and Worthy Consort—all regarded as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tang followed Sui practice: the inner palace ranked Noble Consort, Pure and Fair Consort, Virtuous Consort, and Worthy Consort all as first grade.

sentences.zh: 上欲特置宸妃，以武昭儀為之，韓瑗、來濟諫，以為故事無之，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to establish a special rank of Chen Consort and make the Lady of Bright Deportment Wu it; Han Yuan and Lai Ji remonstrated, saying precedent had none, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to create a new rank, Chen Consort, for Lady Wu; Han Yuan and Lai Ji objected that precedent offered none, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人饒陽李義府為長孫無忌所惡，左遷壁州司馬。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Li Yifu of Raoyang was disliked by Chang Sun Wuji and was transferred left to be prefectural marshal of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu of Raoyang, a secretariat drafter, had earned Chang Sun Wuji's dislike and was demoted to prefectural marshal of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 敕未至門下，義府密知之，問計於中書舍人幽州王德儉，德儉曰：「上欲立武昭儀為后，猶豫未決者，直恐宰臣異議耳。

translations.literal: The edict had not yet reached the Secretariat Office; Yifu secretly learned of it and asked counsel of Secretariat Drafter Wang Dejian of Youzhou. Dejian said: "The emperor wishes to install Lady Wu of Bright Deportment as empress; his hesitance in not deciding is solely fear of the chief ministers' dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict reached the Secretariat, Yifu learned of it in secret and sought counsel from Wang Dejian of Youzhou, another drafter. Dejian said, "The emperor means to make Lady Wu empress but hesitates only because he fears the chief ministers will object.

sentences.zh: 君能建策立之，則轉禍為福矣。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, can propose establishing her, then you will turn misfortune into fortune."
translations.idiomatic: If you propose it yourself, you will turn this disgrace into advancement."

sentences.zh: 義府然之，是日，代德儉直宿，叩閣上表，請廢皇后王氏，立武昭儀，以厭兆庶之心。

translations.literal: Yifu agreed; that day he substituted for Dejian on night duty, knocked at the gate tower and submitted a memorial, requesting to depose Empress Wang and install Lady Wu of Bright Deportment, to satisfy the hearts of the myriad commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu agreed. That day he took Dejian's night watch, knocked at the gate tower, and memorialized to depose Empress Wang, install Lady Wu, and quiet the people's unease.

sentences.zh: 上悅，召見，與語，賜珠一鬥，留居舊職。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, summoned him to audience and conversed, bestowed one peck of pearls, and kept him in his old post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, received him, talked with him, gave a peck of pearls, and kept him in his post.

sentences.zh: 昭儀又密遣使勞勉之，尋超拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment also secretly sent envoys to comfort and encourage him; before long he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu secretly sent envoys to encourage him; soon he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 於是衛尉卿許敬宗、御義大夫崔義玄、中丞袁公瑜皆潛布腹心於武昭儀矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan Xu Jingzong, Grand Master of Imperial Righteousness Cui Yixuan, and Censor Yuan Gongyu all secretly placed trusted hearts with Lady Wu of Bright Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xu Jingzong, chamberlain for the imperial clan, Cui Yixuan, grand master of imperial righteousness, and the censor Yuan Gongyu all secretly pledged themselves to Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以侍中崔敦禮為中書令。

translations.literal: On yiyou, appointed Palace Attendant Cui Dunli as Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Cui Dunli, palace attendant, was made chancellor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八月，尚藥奉御蔣孝璋員外特置，仍同正員。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Palace Physician Jiang Xiaozhang was specially established as supernumerary outside the roster, with rank equal to regular appointee.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Jiang Xiaozhang, palace physician, was specially appointed as supernumerary with rank equal to a regular post.

sentences.zh: 員外同正自孝璋始。

translations.literal: Supernumerary equal to regular began with Xiaozhang.
translations.idiomatic: The title of supernumerary equal to regular appointee began with Xiaozhang.

sentences.zh: 長安令裴行儉聞將立武昭儀為后，以國家之禍必由此始，與長孫無忌、褚遂良私議其事。

translations.literal: Prefect of Chang'an Pei Xingjian heard that Lady Wu of Bright Deportment would be installed as empress; national calamity would surely begin from this—he privately discussed the matter with Chang Sun Wuji and Chu Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian, prefect of Chang'an, heard Lady Wu was to be made empress and believed national disaster would begin there; he discussed it in private with Chang Sun Wuji and Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 袁公瑜聞之，以告昭儀母楊氏，行儉坐左遷西州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Yuan Gongyu heard of it and reported to Lady Yang, the Lady of Bright Deportment's mother; Xingjian was punished by transfer to chief secretary of the Western Prefecture protectorate headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gongyu learned of it and told Lady Yang; Xingjian was demoted to chief secretary of the Western Prefecture protectorate.

sentences.zh: 行儉，仁基之子也。

translations.literal: Xingjian was the son of Pei Rensi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was a son of Pei Rensi.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰，以許敬宗為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on wuchen, appointed Xu Jingzong as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuchen, Xu Jingzong was made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 上一日退朝，召長孫無忌、李勣、於志寧、褚遂良入內殿。

translations.literal: One day the emperor retired from court and summoned Chang Sun Wuji, Li Ji, Yu Zhining, and Chu Suiliang into the inner palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: One day after court the emperor summoned Chang Sun Wuji, Li Ji, Yu Zhining, and Chu Suiliang to the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 遂良曰：「今日之召，多為中宮，上意既決，逆之必死。

translations.literal: Suiliang said: "Today's summons is mostly about the inner palace; the emperor's intent is already decided—to oppose it is surely death.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said, "Today's summons concerns the inner palace; the emperor's mind is set, and to oppose him is death.

sentences.zh: 太尉元舅，司空功臣，不可使上有殺元舅及功臣之名。

translations.literal: The Grand Mentor is the emperor's maternal uncle by marriage, the Minister of Works a merit minister—you cannot let the emperor bear the name of killing a maternal uncle and merit minister.
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's uncle by marriage and a founding minister—you must not let him earn the name of killing kin and merit.

sentences.zh: 遂良起於草茅，無汗馬之勞，致位至此，且受顧托，不以死爭之，何以下見先帝！」

translations.literal: Suiliang rose from humble grass and marsh, without the toil of battle sweat, yet reached this position and moreover received the dying entrustment—if I do not contend with my death, how can I face the late emperor below!"
translations.idiomatic: I rose from the common soil without battlefield merit, yet reached this rank and received the late emperor's dying charge—if I will not stake my life on this, how shall I face him in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 勣稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Li Ji claimed illness and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 無忌等至內殿，上顧謂無忌曰：「皇后無子，武昭儀有子，今欲立昭儀為后，何如？」

translations.literal: Wuji and the others reached the inner hall; the emperor looked at Wuji and said: "The empress has no sons; Lady Wu of Bright Deportment has sons—now I wish to install the Lady of Bright Deportment as empress; how is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the rest entered the inner hall; the emperor turned to Wuji and said, "The empress has no sons, but Lady Wu has borne a son. I mean to make Lady Wu empress. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 遂良對曰：「皇后名家，先帝為陛下所娶。

translations.literal: Suiliang replied: "The empress is of an eminent house; the late emperor married her for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang answered, "The empress comes of an eminent house; the late emperor chose her for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 先帝臨崩，執陛下手謂臣曰：『朕佳兒佳婦，今以付卿。』

translations.literal: At the late emperor's deathbed he held Your Majesty's hand and said to us ministers: 'I leave you my fine son and fine daughter-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: At his deathbed the late emperor took Your Majesty's hand and told us, 'I leave you my fine son and daughter-in-law.'

sentences.zh: 此陛下所聞，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: This Your Majesty heard—his words are still at the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty heard those words yourself; they are still fresh in the ear.

sentences.zh: 皇后未聞有過，豈可輕廢！

translations.literal: The empress has not been heard to have faults—how can she be lightly deposed!
translations.idiomatic: No fault has been heard against the empress—how can she be cast aside so lightly!

sentences.zh: 臣不敢曲從陛下，上違先帝之命！」

translations.literal: I dare not bend to follow Your Majesty and above violate the late emperor's command!"
translations.idiomatic: I dare not bend to Your Majesty's will and violate the late emperor's charge from above!"

sentences.zh: 上不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and broke off the audience.

sentences.zh: 明日又言之，遂良曰：「陛下必欲易皇后，伏請妙擇天下令族，何必武氏！

translations.literal: The next day he spoke of it again; Suiliang said: "If Your Majesty must change empress, I humbly beg you finely choose an eminent clan of the realm—why must it be the Wu clan!
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor raised it again; Suiliang said, "If Your Majesty must replace the empress, I beg you choose some eminent house under heaven—why must it be the Wu clan!

sentences.zh: 武氏經事先帝，眾所共知，天下耳目，安可蔽也。

translations.literal: Lady Wu served the late emperor—this is known to all; the eyes and ears of the realm—how can it be concealed!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu once served the late emperor—a fact everyone knows. The eyes and ears of the realm cannot be hoodwinked.

sentences.zh: 萬代之後，謂陛下為如何！

translations.literal: Ten thousand generations hence, what will they call Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand generations hence, what will history call Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 願留三思！

translations.literal: I beg you reserve further thought!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think again!

sentences.zh: 臣今忤陛下，罪當死！」

translations.literal: I now oppose Your Majesty; the crime deserves death!"
translations.idiomatic: I now defy Your Majesty, and the crime deserves death!

sentences.zh: 因置笏於殿階，解巾叩頭流血曰：「還陛下笏，乞放歸田裡。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he set his tablet on the palace steps, removed his headcloth, and kowtowed until his forehead bled, saying: "I return Your Majesty's tablet and beg to be released to my fields and village."
translations.idiomatic: He laid his court tablet on the palace steps, removed his official headcloth, and kowtowed until blood ran from his forehead, crying, "I return Your Majesty's tablet and beg leave to go home to my fields."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him removed from the hall.

sentences.zh: 昭儀在簾中大言曰：「何不撲殺此獠！」

translations.literal: Lady Zhao shouted from behind the curtain: "Why not beat this brute to death!"
translations.idiomatic: From behind the curtain Lady Wu cried out, "Why not beat this wretch to death!"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「遂良受先朝顧命，有罪不可加刑！」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "Suiliang received the late emperor's dying charge; though guilty, he may not be punished with corporal penalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Suiliang bore the late emperor's final charge. Even if he is guilty, he must not be subjected to physical punishment!"

sentences.zh: 於志寧不敢言。

translations.literal: Yu Zhining did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 韓瑗因間奏事，涕泣極諫，上不納。

translations.literal: Han Yuan seized an occasion to present business, wept, and remonstrated to the utmost; the emperor would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan found an opening to address the throne, wept, and pleaded with all his strength, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 明日又諫，悲不自勝，上命引出。

translations.literal: The next day he remonstrated again, grief overcoming him beyond bearing; the emperor ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he remonstrated again until he was overcome with grief, and the emperor had him escorted out.

sentences.zh: 瑗又上疏諫曰：「匹夫匹婦，猶相選擇，況天子乎！

translations.literal: Yuan again submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "Common men and women still choose one another—how much more the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan submitted another memorial: "Even common husbands and wives choose their mates—how much more must the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 皇后母儀萬國，善惡由之，故嫫母輔佐黃帝，妲己傾覆殷王，《詩》云：『赫赫宗周，褒姒滅之。』

translations.literal: The empress is the motherly model for ten thousand states; good and evil follow from her. Therefore Mo Mu assisted the Yellow Emperor, Daji overturned the Yin king, and the Odes say: 'Splendid was the house of Zhou—Bao Si destroyed it.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress is the motherly exemplar of the realm, and good and evil flow from her. Mo Mu aided the Yellow Emperor; Daji brought down the Yin dynasty. The Odes say, 'Splendid was the house of Zhou—until Bao Si destroyed it.'

sentences.zh: 每覽前古，常興歎息，不謂今日塵黷聖代。

translations.literal: Whenever I read of antiquity I always sigh deeply; I never thought that today would stain and defile this sacred age.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read of the past I sigh—and never imagined that today would bring such stain upon this sacred age.

sentences.zh: 作而不法，後嗣何觀！

translations.literal: To act without regard to law—what will posterity have to look upon!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty acts without regard to law, what will posterity have to look upon!

sentences.zh: 願陛下詳之，無為後人所笑！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would consider this carefully and not be laughed at by those who come after!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully and not become a laughingstock to later ages!

sentences.zh: 使臣有以益國，菹醢之戮，臣之分也！

translations.literal: If I can in any way benefit the state, execution by mincing is my proper portion!
translations.idiomatic: If I can in any way serve the state, death by dismemberment is my proper due!

sentences.zh: 昔吳王不用子胥之言而麋鹿游於姑蘇。

translations.literal: Formerly the king of Wu did not use Zixu's words, and deer roamed the terraces of Gusu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the king of Wu ignored Zixu's counsel, and deer grazed among the terraces of Gusu.

sentences.zh: 臣恐海內失望，棘荊生於闕庭，宗廟不血食，期有日矣！」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that within the seas hope will fail, brambles will grow in the palace courtyard, and the ancestral temple will go without blood offerings—the day cannot be far off!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear the realm will lose heart, brambles will grow in the palace courts, and the ancestral temple will go without sacrifice—and that day cannot be far off!"

sentences.zh: 來濟上表諫曰：「王者立后，上法乾坤，必擇禮教名家，幽閒令淑，副四海之望，稱神示氏之意。

translations.literal: Lai Ji submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "When a king establishes an empress, he takes Heaven and Earth as his model above and must choose a family renowned in ritual and teaching, secluded, refined, and virtuous, matching the hopes of the four seas and fulfilling the intent shown by the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji submitted a memorial: "When a king establishes an empress, he takes Heaven and Earth as his model and must choose a family steeped in ritual and virtue—a woman secluded, refined, and worthy of the realm's hopes and of the spirits' intent.

sentences.zh: 是故周文造舟以迎太姒，而興《關雎》之化，百姓蒙祚；

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen of Zhou built a boat to welcome Taisi, and the transformation of "Guan Ju" arose, and the common people received blessing;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou built a boat to welcome Taisi, and the virtue celebrated in "Guan Ju" flourished, bringing blessing to the people;

sentences.zh: 孝成縱欲，以婢為后，使皇統亡絕，社稷傾淪。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng of Han indulged his desires, made a maidservant empress, and caused the imperial line to perish and the altars of state to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng indulged his desires, made a maidservant empress, and brought the imperial line to ruin and the state to collapse.

sentences.zh: 有周之隆既如彼，大漢之禍又如此，惟陛下詳察！」

translations.literal: The prosperity of Zhou was thus, and the calamity of Han was likewise—may Your Majesty examine this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's glory stood thus, and Han's disaster likewise—may Your Majesty weigh this carefully!"

sentences.zh: 上皆不納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected all of it.

sentences.zh: 它日，李勣入見，上問之曰：「朕欲立武昭儀為后，遂良固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Another day, Li Ji entered audience. The emperor asked him: "I wish to make Lady Wu Zhao empress, but Suiliang stubbornly holds that it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Li Ji came to audience. The emperor asked, "I wish to make Lady Wu empress, but Suiliang stubbornly insists it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 遂良既顧命大臣，事當且已乎？」

translations.literal: Suiliang is after all a minister charged at the late emperor's deathbed—should the matter simply be dropped?"
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was entrusted at the late emperor's deathbed—should I simply let the matter drop?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此陛下家事，何必更問外人！」

translations.literal: He replied: "This is Your Majesty's family affair—why must you ask outsiders again!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "This is Your Majesty's own household matter—why ask outsiders at all!"

sentences.zh: 上意遂決。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗宣言於朝曰：「田舍翁多收十斛麥，尚欲易婦；

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong declared openly at court: "A rustic who has harvested ten more hu of wheat still wants to change wives;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong declared openly at court, "A farmer who harvests ten extra bushels of wheat still wants a new wife;

sentences.zh: 況天子欲立一后，何豫諸人事而妄生異議乎！」

translations.literal: how much more when the Son of Heaven wishes to establish an empress—what business is it of others to meddle and raise objections in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: how much more when the Son of Heaven wishes to make an empress—what business is it of others to raise objections!"

sentences.zh: 昭儀令左右以聞。

translations.literal: Lady Zhao ordered those at her side to report this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu had her attendants report this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 庚午，貶遂良為潭州都督。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Suiliang was demoted to protector-general of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, Suiliang was demoted to protector-general of Tan Prefecture.
